# PocketOne

> PocketOne is a community fork of PocketBase (one Go binary: database, auth, files, realtime, admin UI) with extensions for point-in-time recovery, backups, mail, many instances on one server, deploys, tokens and OAuth, MCP, and PocketPages server-rendered sites.

PocketOne takes the same commands and flags as PocketBase, plus its own; core PocketBase topics live at https://pocketbase.io/docs. Agent Skills for PocketOne and PocketPages: https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/agent (Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add pockethost/pocketone`).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/overview

# What is PocketOne?

PocketOne is a community fork of [PocketBase](https://pocketbase.io). It tracks upstream PocketBase and keeps its own
changes to the core small: only the hooks that let extensions extend and override PocketBase. Every feature lives in an
extension.

It's maintained by [PocketHost](https://pockethost.io), which runs it in production. PocketOne is not affiliated with
or endorsed by the PocketBase project.

## How it's built

- **A small core.** PocketBase's own code changes only to add hooks. Each change is marked in the source, reviewed by
  someone who didn't write it, and kept minimal so upstream releases merge cleanly.
- **Everything else is an extension.** Extensions live in `ext/` in the repo. Each is its own Go module, with a README and a
  small example.
- **Off until you use it.** The extensions in the `pocketone` binary add no work to an app that doesn't use them.
- **One app or hundreds.** An extension written against the extension contract works the same on a single app and on every
  instance under a multi-instance host.

## Open to contributions

PocketOne is open to everyone. Ask questions and share ideas in
[GitHub Discussions](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/discussions), report bugs in
[Issues](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/issues), and send extensions as pull requests. Start with
[Writing an extension](https://pocketone.dev/docs/writing-an-extension).

## Where to next

- [Install PocketOne](https://pocketone.dev/docs/installation)
- [See what PocketOne adds to PocketBase](https://pocketone.dev/docs/what-pocketone-adds)
- [Browse the extensions](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions)


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/installation

# Installation

PocketOne is one executable, `pocketone`. It is built on PocketBase v0.41 and takes the same commands and flags, plus its own.

## Homebrew (macOS and Linux)

```bash
brew install pockethost/tap/pocketone
```

The formula lives in [pockethost/homebrew-tap](https://github.com/pockethost/homebrew-tap).

## Download a release

Download the zip for your platform from
[Releases](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/releases), unzip it, and put `pocketone` somewhere on your `PATH`.

## Build from source

With [Go](https://go.dev) installed:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone.git
cd pocketone/examples/pocketone
go build -o pocketone .
```

## Run it

Create your first superuser before the first serve:

```bash
pocketone superuser upsert <email> <password>
pocketone serve
```

Opening `http://127.0.0.1:8090/_/` to create it also works, as in PocketBase.

To start a site with server-rendered pages:

```bash
pocketone pages create myapp
cd myapp
pocketone serve --dev --dir ./pb_data
```

In dev mode (`serve --dev`), an app with no SMTP settings doesn't send mail through the system's `sendmail`. PocketOne
catches the mail and shows it at `http://127.0.0.1:8025`.

## Upgrade

```bash
pocketone upgrade
```

This replaces the executable with the latest release. The old one is kept beside it as `pocketone-<version>`, never
deleted, so you can go back.

## Moving from PocketBase

PocketOne reads the same `pb_data`, `pb_hooks`, `pb_migrations` and `pb_public` folders. Point it at your existing data
directory with `--dir`, as you would with `pocketbase`. Back up `pb_data` first.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/what-pocketone-adds

# What PocketOne adds

Run `pocketone` the way you run `pocketbase`. These are the differences you'll notice.

## Point-in-time restore, on by default

Your database is replicated with Litestream, so you can restore it to any moment from **Settings → Backups** or with
`pocketone pitr restore`. Turn it off with `--pitr=false`.

## Mail you can see in dev mode

In dev mode (`serve --dev`), an app with no SMTP settings doesn't send through the system's `sendmail`. The mail is
caught and shown at `http://127.0.0.1:8025`.

## Server-rendered pages

Put `.ejs` and Markdown files in a `pb_pages` folder and they're served as pages, with no build step. This site is
one. `pocketone pages create myapp` starts a new site from a starter kit. Full docs are at
[pocketpages.dev](https://pocketpages.dev).

## A config file

Settings can live in `pocketone.yaml`, with secrets in a `.env` file beside it that your JS hooks never see. Without
the file, PocketOne behaves like stock PocketBase. `pocketone config` lists every section, and
`pocketone config check` checks a file. The [config reference](https://pocketone.dev/docs/config-reference) lists every section.

## Commands for working with remote apps

- `pocketone login`, `remote` and `link`: save logins to your apps.
- `pocketone deploy`, `dev`, `pull` and `logs`: ship `pb_hooks`, `pb_migrations` and `pb_public` to an app and
  watch it.
- `pocketone upgrade`: move to the latest release, keeping the old executable.

## Agents and API tokens

- An MCP endpoint at `/mcp` lets agents such as Claude manage your app and call its tools.
- Long-lived API tokens (`pbt_…`) with scopes, for scripts and integrations.
- Your app can act as an OAuth provider; `pocketone login` and MCP sign-in use it.

## Extensions that fit together

PocketOne's extensions meet through contracts: named, versioned promises like `restore/v1` that any extension can
keep. The dashboard, the `pocketone` command, agents and your `pb_hooks` call the contract, so you can swap the
extension behind it without changing anything else. [How PocketOne fits together](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts) explains it.

## Everything else

Automatic TLS certificates, bulk mail to your own users, scheduled VACUUM, signed S3 download redirects, and more. See
[all extensions](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions).

## What stays the same

The admin dashboard, collections, rules, the REST and realtime APIs, JS hooks and migrations all work as in PocketBase.
For those, the [PocketBase docs](https://pocketone.dev/docs/pocketbase) are the reference.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/agents

# Coding agents

PocketOne is new, so coding agents haven't seen much of it. Two things close that gap. Both are built from these docs, so they change when the docs change.

## Agent Skills

The `pocketone` plugin has two skills:

- **pocketone:** the `pocketone` binary and its commands, `pocketone.yaml`, every extension, and writing your own extension with contracts.
- **pocketpages:** building PocketPages v1 sites in `pb_pages/`: routing, `ctx`, templates, layouts, auth and deploying.

Each skill carries a copy of the docs in its `reference/` folder, so it works offline.

**Claude Code**

```
/plugin marketplace add pockethost/pocketone
/plugin install pocketone@pocketone
```

`/plugin marketplace update pocketone` picks up new versions.

**Other agents that read Agent Skills** (Cursor, Codex, Gemini CLI and others)

```bash
npx skills add pockethost/pocketone
```

Or copy a skill folder into your project yourself. The skills live in [`agent/skills/`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/agent/skills).

## llms.txt

For agents and tools that read the web:

- [pocketone.dev/llms.txt](https://pocketone.dev/llms.txt) indexes every docs page with a one-line summary.
- [pocketone.dev/llms-full.txt](https://pocketone.dev/llms-full.txt) holds every docs page in one Markdown file.

PocketPages has its own at [pocketpages.dev/llms.txt](https://pocketpages.dev/llms.txt) and [pocketpages.dev/llms-full.txt](https://pocketpages.dev/llms-full.txt).

# Extensions

Each extension is a Go module in [`ext/`](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/ext) with its own README; the pages here are those READMEs. Want to add one? Read [Writing an extension](https://pocketone.dev/docs/writing-an-extension).

## Standard extensions

These ship with `pocketone` and add no work to an app that doesn't use them.

| Extension | What it does |
|---|---|
| [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr) | Point-in-time restore of your database with Litestream. On by default. |
| [Settings](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/settings) | One API for the settings an app's admins change for its extensions. On by default. |
| [Backups](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/backups) | Restore an app to a moment from its own backups: the latest one before it. On by default. |
| [Auto TLS](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/autotls) | Certificates on demand and wildcards through ACME. |
| [Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail) | Campaigns to your app's own users, with audiences from a collection, a view or SQL. |
| [Pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages) | Server-rendered pages from a pb_pages folder (formerly PocketPages). |
| [Vacuum](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/vacuum) | Planned. Scheduled SQLite VACUUM. |
| [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) | An MCP endpoint at /mcp so agents can manage your app and call its tools. |
| [S3 Redirect](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3redirect) | File downloads as short-lived signed S3 redirects. |
| [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) | Long-lived API tokens with scopes. |
| [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | pocketone deploy, dev, pull and logs, and the deploy API. |
| [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes) | Named remotes and saved logins for the pocketone command. |
| [Upgrade](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/upgrade) | pocketone upgrade to the latest release, keeping the old executable. |
| [Config](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/config) | The pocketone.yaml config file, with secrets in a .env beside it. |
| [JSVM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/jsvm) | PocketOne's JS engine: one QuickJS VM per app, real globals, async handlers, hard limits. |

## Run many instances

Host hundreds of PocketBase instances in one process, across regions.

| Extension | What it does |
|---|---|
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | Hundreds of PocketBase instances in one Go process, routed by hostname. |
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | Many instances behind one listener, routed by hostname, run by one provider. |
| [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) | A host provider that runs each instance in its own container. |
| [Sandbox](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/sandbox) | Confines untrusted JS hooks, SQL and outbound network. |
| [Firewall](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall) | Peer allow-lists, trusted proxies and rate limits for a host. |
| [Edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge) | Forwards each request to the edge that owns the instance. |
| [Mothership](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mothership) | A control plane and its edges, across regions. |
| [Schedules](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/schedules) | Planned. Scheduled webhooks that wake sleeping instances. |
| [Stats](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/stats) | Measures disk use and last request for each instance a host serves. |

## Services for your instances

Shared services a host gives every instance it runs.

| Extension | What it does |
|---|---|
| [Mail Relay](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailrelay) | Outgoing mail for instances without SMTP, through your relay, with limits. |
| [S3 Fallback](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3-fallback) | A default bucket for uploads and backups when an instance has no S3 of its own. |
| [Server Timing](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/servertiming) | Server-Timing headers for each step of a request. |
| [WASM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/wasm) | Bring your own WASM: Go, Rust or Zig plugins called from pb_hooks, each a closed box. |

## Sell it as a service

Accounts, quotas and billing, for running PocketBase as a service.

| Extension | What it does |
|---|---|
| [Multitenant](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tenants) | Planned. Accounts that own instances: quotas, owner logins, tokens and an API. |
| [Multitenant Billing](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tenant-billing) | Planned. Plans, quotas and the billing provider hook for Multitenant. |
| [Lemon Squeezy Adapter](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tenant-billing-ls) | Planned. Lemon Squeezy as the billing provider. |

## For extension authors

The extension contract and tools for building and testing extensions.

| Extension | What it does |
|---|---|
| [Extension Kit](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/extkit/extkit.go) | The extension contract: one extension works on a single app and under pocker. |
| [Standard Set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard) | The extensions every PocketOne app has, as one set a host configures. |
| [Contracts](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/README.md) | The versioned interfaces extensions use to work together, and the generator that writes their plumbing. |
| [Mail Trap](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailtrap) | Dev mode: mail from an app without SMTP lands in a built-in inbox. |
| [Dev Users](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/devusers/devusers.go) | Local testing only: a superuser and a user with password "password". |
| [Bundle](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bundle) | An app's hooks, migrations and public files embedded in the binary. |


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/writing-an-extension

# Create your own extension

A PocketOne extension is Go code compiled into your build. There are two kinds, by where they run:

- **App extensions** add to an app: Go routes, PocketBase hooks, collections, admin dashboard screens, a JS API for
  `pb_hooks`, contracts other extensions use. They run on every app: a standalone app, or each instance of a
  multisite host. Almost every extension is one.
- **Host extensions** add to a multisite host, the process that serves many instances: request gates (firewall, rate
  limits), TLS, middleware around every instance, instance sources, background jobs.

How a multisite host runs its instances (in-process with [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker), in containers with
[docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker), or both) is the host's `runtime/v1` contract. App extensions don't depend on it.

## App extensions: `extkit`

Write an extension once, against [`extkit`](../ext/extkit/extkit.go) (its own module,
`github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit`; core has no part in it), and the same value runs on every app:

```go
type Extension struct{ cfg Config }

func New(cfg Config) *Extension { return &Extension{cfg: cfg} }

func (p *Extension) Name() string { return "hello" } // config key, `_hello_` collections, logs

func (p *Extension) Register(app core.App, cfg extkit.Config) error {
    c := p.cfg
    if err := cfg.Decode(&c); err != nil { // this app's settings over the defaults (json tags)
        return err
    }
    app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(se *core.ServeEvent) error { /* routes, UI extensions */ return se.Next() })
    return nil
}

// optional: a $hello global in the app's JS hooks
func (p *Extension) BindJS(app core.App, rt js.Runtime) { /* rt.Set("$hello", ...) */ }

// optional: its TypeScript declarations, added to each app's pb_data/types.d.ts
func (p *Extension) TypeScript() string { return `declare var $hello: { greet(name: string): string };` }
```

- **Every app has the [standard set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard)** (tokens, mcp, pitr, deploy and the rest). Add yours
  to it: `set.Add(myextension.New(...))`. On a standalone app, build the app with `set.NewApp(...)`, or build it
  yourself and call `set.Register(app, jsvm.Config{...})`. The stock binary does the second: `pocketbase.NewWithConfig`,
  then `set.Register` ([`examples/pocketone`](../examples/pocketone/main.go)). Without the set:
  `extkit.MustRegister(app, extensions...)`, and `extkit.BindJS(app, vm, extensions...)` in jsvm's `OnInit`.
- **On a multisite host** every instance gets the set, with that instance's `extensions.<name>` settings over your
  constructor's defaults. `enabled: false` there means `Register` and `BindJS` are never called for that instance.
  What runs inside an instance depends on its runtime: pocker registers the set in-process; a docker instance runs
  the `pocketone` binary in its container, so it has the stock set (your own extras need your own image); an instance
  on a stock PocketBase image runs none, and gets only the contracts the host provides for it
  ([Working together](#working-together-contracts)).
- **Routes:** an extension has none of its own. Its API is contracts, mounted for you under `/api/_c/<id>/`; design
  the contract in `ext/contracts` first ([Working together](#working-together-contracts)). Admin settings go through
  `settings/v1` (`settingsv1.Add`). Only paths a standard fixes stay at the root (`/.well-known/*`, `/mcp`). The
  conformance test fails any other route unless `conformance.Options.AllowRoutes` lists it with a reason.
- **Process-wide settings** come from a `pocketone.yaml` section your extension owns (`extkit.NewSection`).
- **State per app:** keep it in `app.Store()`. Something shared across apps (a pool, a client) closes through
  `extkit.Closer`.
- **Name the command with `extkit.Command`:** when a message tells people what to run ("run 'pocketone login
  prod'"), build it from `extkit.Command` (default `pocketone`), never a literal. A build shipped under another name
  (PocketHost's, say) sets it once in `main`, or with `-ldflags "-X github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit.Command=pockethost"`.
- [bulkmail](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/bulkmail/extension.go) is the reference implementation, and
  [`ext/standard/example`](../ext/standard/example/main.go) a complete program.

## Working together: contracts

> Start with [How PocketOne fits together](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts) for the idea: every API an extension offers is a named,
> versioned contract, any extension can provide one, and everything else (the dashboard, the CLI, agents, `pb_hooks`,
> other extensions) calls the contract, never the extension. This section is how to do it in code.

In short, when you design an extension:

1. **Find the contracts you need** in the [catalogue](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/all). Use them; don't reach into another
   extension.
2. **Decide what you offer.** Anything a client calls is a contract. If one already promises it, provide that one
   (your extension then stands in for the current provider). If not, write the contract first, named for what it
   does, not for your extension.
3. **Declare it** in `Contracts()` and **provide it** in `Register`. The startup lines, whoami and the catalogue show
   it from then on.

Extensions never depend on each other by name. They depend on **contracts**: versioned Go interfaces in
[`ext/contracts`](../ext/contracts/README.md), such as `deploy/v1` or `mail.fallback/v1`. Every API an extension
offers is a contract too, served at `/api/_c/<id>/`: extensions have no routes of their own.

Every contract, standard or community, lives in `ext/contracts/<id path>/vN/` with a README like an extension's
(owners and a one-line summary in its front matter; `## Use`, `## Provide`, `## Extensions`, `## License`). Its
Extensions section is generated from every extension's `Contracts()`: who provides it, requires it and works with
it (`go run ./.github/extensions contracts`; CI fails when it's stale or when an extension names a contract that
doesn't exist). Whoever first creates a contract owns it, so an extension author who adds one owns both. Design the
contract first, then the extension that provides it.

An extension declares what it implements, requires and works with:

```go
func (e *Extension) Contracts() extkit.Contracts {
    return extkit.Contracts{
        Implements: extkit.IDs("deploy/v1"),
        Defaults:   extkit.IDs("deploy/v1"), // steps aside if another extension provides it
        WorksWith:  extkit.IDs("tokens/v1"), // used when present
    }
}

func (e *Extension) Register(app core.App, cfg extkit.Config) error {
    deployv1.Contract.ProvideDefault(app, myDeployer{})
    return nil
}
```

At startup PocketOne resolves every contract and prints who provides it:

```
standard: deploy/v1 ← fastdeploy (default deploy stepped aside)
standard: bulkmail off: needs mail.fallback/v1, which nothing provides
```

- **Look contracts up after registration** (in hooks, at serve time): `deployv1.Contract.Must(app)`. A lookup inside
  `Register` panics.
- **Defaults, conflicts, choices.** A default steps aside for any other provider. Two other providers of a contract that
  allows one fail the start until `pocketone.yaml` picks one (`providers: { mail.fallback/v1: mailrelay }`).
- **Wrappers** decorate whatever provides a contract (`Contract.Wrap`), in registration order.
- **Wire contracts** have an HTTP API at `/api/_c/<id>/<op>`, action hooks in Go (`deployv1.OnUpload`) and JS
  (`onDeployUpload`), an MCP tool per operation and a client. Every caller passes the same scope check and hooks.
- **From pb_hooks:** an app's JS declares and provides its contracts in `onContracts`, which runs once after
  `pb_hooks` load and before the seal (so before bootstrap):

  ```js
  onContracts((e) => {
    e.provide("mail.fallback/v1", { send(m) { /* ... */ } }) // a contract open to JS
    e.require("restore/v1")   // the start fails (dev mode: warns) when nothing provides it
    e.worksWith("tokens/v1")  // shown in the startup lines
    e.next()
  })
  ```

  The startup lines show it (`pb_hooks: provides mail.fallback/v1; requires restore/v1`). Methods run on pooled
  runtimes like any hook handler, so they can't use the file's local variables. A Go extension that *requires* a
  contract only JS provides is resolved before the JS runs: name `pb_hooks` under `providers:` for it in
  `pocketone.yaml`.
- **CLI:** every operation of a wire contract is a `pocketone remote ...` command with no code (`remote restore to
  --at -2h`), flags from its input. Provide [cli.commands/v1](../ext/contracts/cli/commands/v1/README.md) to replace
  one with your own, or to add one (`remote rehash`).
- **No imports between extensions.** An extension imports `extkit` and contract packages, never another extension's
  module (tests and examples may). What it needs from another goes in the contract package: tokens/v1 has
  `RegisterScope`, `FromRequest` and `WithScopes`; remote/v1 has its CLI client (`remoteclient`), which deploy's
  commands use.

## Compiled in, not loaded at run time

Extensions are Go packages linked into the binary, the way Caddy modules work. Go's `plugin` package (`.so` files)
isn't used:
- it needs identical toolchain and dependency versions;
- it can't unload;
- it rules out static `CGO_ENABLED=0` builds.

A build is a small `main.go`: the standard set with your extensions added, as a standalone app or a multisite host.

## Your module

PocketOne keeps PocketBase's module path, so upstream merges stay clean. Point it at PocketOne in your `go.mod`:

```
require ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase v0.41.1

replace ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase => github.com/pockethost/pocketone <commit or version>
```

Go only honors `replace` in the main module, so the final binary's `go.mod` needs this line, not only your
extension's.

## Admin screens: `UIExtensions`

The dashboard loads extensions before it starts its router:
- Each extension is a named file system served at `/_/extensions/<name>/`.
- Every extension's `main.js` is bundled into `/_/extensions.js`.

Add yours in the same `OnServe` hook:

```go
//go:embed ui
var uiFiles embed.FS

ui, _ := fs.Sub(uiFiles, "ui")
se.UIExtensions = append(se.UIExtensions, core.UIExtension{Name: "hello", FS: ui})
```

`ui/main.js` runs in the dashboard with its UI kit (`t.*`) and globals (`app.routes`, `app.store`, `app.pb`):

```js
// a new page, with a link in the header
app.routes.superuserOnly("#/hello", async () => {
    const res = await app.pb.send("/api/hello");
    return t.div({ className: "page" },
        t.div({ className: "page-content" }, t.h1({}, "Hello"), t.p({}, `Instance ${res.instance}`)),
    );
});
app.store.headerLinks.push({ href: "#/hello", icon: "ri-emotion-happy-line", label: "Hello" });

// add to an existing screen: screens marked with pbEvent fire mount:<name> with their element
document.addEventListener("mount:pageBackupsSettings", (e) => {
    e.detail.prepend(t.p({ className: "txt-hint" }, "Hello from an extension."));
});
```

- **More hooks:** `app.store.settingsNavGroups` adds entries to the Settings sidebar. Search `pbEvent:` in
  [`ui/src`](../ui/src) for every screen you can add to (Backups exposes `pageBackupsSettings`, `backupsList`,
  `backupsSettingsForm`, `backupCreateModal` and `backupRestoreModal`).
- **No build step:** plain JS works. Bundle with Vite if you prefer.
- **Experimental upstream:** this UI extension API is undocumented and can change between PocketBase releases
  (`ui/README.md`). Keep `main.js` small, and test it after each upstream update.

## Host extensions

A multisite host is one process serving many instances. A host extension works on that process, for every instance.
Like app extensions, host extensions work together through contracts, on the host's own scope:

| Concern | Contract | Providers |
|---|---|---|
| What runs the instances (one or several, in preference order) | [runtime/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/runtime/v1) | [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker), [docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) |
| Which instances exist (the instance record) | [instance.source/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/instance.source/v1) | `instances.yaml` (default), [mothership](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mothership) |
| Admit requests (firewall, rate limits) | [gate/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/gate/v1) | [firewall](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall) |
| TLS for the host's listener | [tls/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/tls/v1) | [autotls](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/autotls) |
| Middleware around everything | [http.wrap/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/http.wrap/v1) | [servertiming](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/servertiming) |

A host extension is a `multisite.Extension`: `Name()` and `RegisterHost(h)`, which provides its contracts on
`h.Scope` and provides nothing when it isn't configured (no section). Pass it in `multisite.Options.Extensions` (in
preference order), or `multisite.Link` it from an `init` so linking its package is enough. The host seals its scope
once, with `providers:` choices for host contracts, and logs who provides what:

```go
h, err := multisite.FromConfig(multisite.Options{Choices: providers, Extensions: []multisite.Extension{
	servertiming.New(),         // http.wrap/v1, outermost
	autotls.New(),              // tls/v1 from the `autotls` section
	&pocker.Provider{},         // runtime/v1
	&docker.Provider{},         // runtime/v1 too, when there's a `docker` section
}})
```

```
multisite: runtime/v1 ← pocker, docker
multisite: tls/v1 ← autotls
```

Background work goes on `h.Background`, and an extension with `Close(ctx) error` is closed once every app has
stopped.

Some contracts are provided by the host for its instances (host-provided contracts), because the instance can't
answer them itself: docker runs stock PocketBase images, so the host answers remote/v1 for them. The host serves them
in `h.InstanceRoutes`, which run after the peer check, the blocked answer and the gates (firewall, rate limits) and
before the runtime, with the resolved instance in `multisite.InstanceOf(r)`:

```go
remotev1.Contract.ProvideForInstances(h.Scope, myRemote)
h.InstanceRoutes = append(h.InstanceRoutes, func(next http.Handler) http.Handler {
	return remotev1.W.HostHandler(h.Scope, multisite.InstanceID, myAuth, next)
})
``` Other servers in the fleet are [edge](../ext/edge) (`edge.EdgeSource`, the host's `Forward`), and
runtime-only hooks are pocker's `Starter`, `SetupApp`, `OnStart`, `OnEvent` and `Manager`
([POCKER.md](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker/pocker#extensions)).

App extensions that only need settings shared by every instance (mailrelay, s3-fallback, pitr) read their own
`pocketone.yaml` section on first use and stay app extensions: they work on any host and on a single app.

## Rules on a multisite host

On a multisite host, instances can belong to people who don't trust each other, and your Go code runs with the host's
full power, outside the JS sandbox:
- **Act only for the app you were called for.** Keep per-app state in `app.Store()`, and use `extkit.AppID(app)` for
  anything shared that must differ per instance (a bucket prefix, a rate-limit key); never build a path from request
  input.
- **Instance data needs instance auth.** Protect routes that read or change it with PocketBase's auth middlewares
  (`apis.RequireSuperuserAuth()`, record auth).
- **Exposing something to JS is a sandbox decision.** Expose a function to an instance's JS only if it's safe for a
  hostile tenant to call. See [How is this safe?](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/sandbox#how-is-this-safe).
- **Outbound calls follow the egress policy.** Go's default HTTP client already refuses private addresses. If your
  extension must reach a private service, give it its own `http.Client` and transport, and never let instance input pick
  the address.

## Contributing an extension

Extensions are welcome, from us and from you. Open a pull request that adds `ext/<your-extension>/`.

### Change PocketBase's core as little as possible

PocketOne stays close to upstream so every PocketBase release merges cleanly. If your extension needs something the
core doesn't offer yet:
- **Add the smallest hook that makes it possible:** an extension point or an override, not your extension's logic. A
  nil-checked function field, a list callers can append to, or an event, with upstream behavior unchanged when nothing
  is registered.
- **Make it generic.** Name it for what it allows ("storage backend for an app"), not for your extension. Assume someone
  else's extension will use it too, and that we'll offer it to upstream PocketBase.
- **Mark every changed line** in PocketBase's own files with `// PocketOne:` and a few words on why, so the next upstream
  merge knows what to keep.
- **Keep it separate:** the core change goes in its own commit, with a test, ahead of the extension.
- **Prefer what exists:** jsvm `OnInit`, `OnServe`, the record and request hooks, `BaseAppConfig.DBConnect`,
  `UIExtensions`. Many extensions need no core change at all.

### What an extension folder contains

```
ext/<name>/
  go.mod            module github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/<name>
  README.md         the extension's docs, and its page on pocketone.dev (below)
  <name>.go         the extension
  <name>_test.go
  conformance_test.go  the shared extension test (below)
  example/main.go   a minimal program that builds cleanly and shows the feature
  ui/               optional: admin screens (embedded main.js)
```

- **`example/main.go` is required.** Keep it as small as possible: just enough to build a binary that shows the
  feature working, with no extra harness. `go build ./example` and `go vet ./...` must pass with no warnings.
  [`ext/standard/example`](../ext/standard/example) and [`ext/sandbox/example`](../ext/sandbox/example) are the size to aim for.
- **Examples come with two logins:** superuser `admin@example.com` and user `user@example.com` (verified, in
  `users`), both with password `password`. Every `example/main.go` calls
  `devusers.Register(app)` right after the app is created (on a multisite host, `devusers.Ensure(app)` in the
  host's per-instance setup), from [`ext/devusers`](../ext/devusers/devusers.go). A fresh data dir is then ready to log
  in to, with no installer page and no CLI step. Never register it in a production build.
- **`conformance_test.go` is required.** It runs the shared extension test from
  [`ext/extkit/conformance`](../ext/extkit/conformance/conformance.go) once:

  ```go
  func TestConformance(t *testing.T) {
  	conformance.Run(t, func() extkit.Extension { return myextension.New(myextension.Config{}) })
  }
  ```

  It checks that the extension registers, migrates, serves and shuts down on a fresh app with no goroutines left
  behind; that its only routes are contracts' (`/api/_c/<id>/`); that PocketBase's own collections are unchanged and every collection it adds is named `_<name>` or `_<name>_…`; and
  that one extension value serves several apps at once (as on a multisite host) without registering on one app
  touching another's hooks. An extension that requires another (`Contracts().Requires`) lists it in
  `conformance.Options{Deps: ...}`. An extension that adds MCP tools ([`ext/mcp`](../ext/mcp/README.md#tools-from-an-extension)) also passes
  `conformance.Options{Setup: ...}` that registers MCP on the test apps; the test then checks each tool is named
  `<name>_<verb>_<noun>`, is described, and has an object input schema (`pb_` is reserved). Run it with `go test -race`. It's the minimum every extension passes; your own tests cover the
  feature.
- **The README starts with front matter**: who owns the extension and its version (see [Ownership](#ownership)).

  ```markdown
  ---
  owners: ["@your-github-handle"]
  version: 0.1.0
  ---
  ```

- **The README has five required sections**, in this order. It is also your extension's page on pocketone.dev.
  - `## Install`: how to get it (built into `pocketone`, or the lines to add to a Go build).
  - `## Configure`: the `pocketone.yaml` section, flags and settings screens. The site adds a table of your section's
    keys, generated from your `extkit.NewSection` defaults; describe each key with a `doc:"…"` struct tag.
  - `## Use`: day to day: the admin screens and what to click, the commands.
  - `## Integrations`: the extensions yours works with and how (multisite hosting goes here, not in the sections
    above), and how other extensions can build on yours (hooks, filesystem kinds, per-instance settings, Go
    and REST APIs).
  - `## Example`: the code that uses it. A sentence on what your `example/main.go` runs, then the whole file in a
    ```` ```go ```` block, exactly as it is; `go run ./.github/extensions examples` copies it in, and CI fails when the two
    differ. Without an example (an extension built into `pocketone`), say where to see it used.

  Write the first three for someone running one PocketOne app, not for a Go developer. Anything else (how it works,
  limits) goes in sections after these, and extra guides can sit next to the README as other `.md` files.
- **Extensions here are MIT.** The README ends with `## License` and the single line `MIT`. An extension under another
  license lives in its author's own repository, not here.
  Add your extension to [`site/extensions.json`](../site/extensions.json) and run `cd site/sync && go run .` to build its page.
  [`ext/pitr/README.md`](../ext/pitr/README.md) is the example to follow.
- **CI enforces all of this.** [`.github/workflows/extensions.yml`](../.github/workflows/extensions.yml) fails when an extension
  README is missing its owners and version, one of the five sections or its MIT `## License`, or its Example doesn't match `example/main.go`, or when a module that implements `extkit.Extension` has no conformance
  test, then builds, vets and runs `go test -race` on every module the
  change affects: the modules it touches, every module that reaches one of them through a `replace`, or all of them
  for a core change. Run the same checks locally from the repository root:

  ```bash
  go run ./.github/extensions check
  go run ./.github/extensions affected origin/main HEAD
  ```

  Tests that need an external tool (MinIO, Docker) skip themselves when it isn't installed, so they don't block CI.
- **Dependencies stay in your module.** Heavy libraries go in your extension's `go.mod`, never in core's.
- **Standalone first.** Where it makes sense, an extension works on one standalone app, and adds more on a multisite
  host.
- **MIT**, like PocketBase and the rest of this repo.

### Ownership

Every extension and every contract has owners, listed in its README's front matter (GitHub handles); an extension
also has a version there. Whoever submits an extension or first creates a contract owns it, so an author who adds a
contract with their extension owns both.

Who approves an outside pull request:

| What it changes | Who approves |
|---|---|
| PocketBase's own code, the standard extensions, the site, docs, examples, CI | a maintainer |
| A community extension | one of its owners, or a maintainer |
| A contract | one of its owners, or a maintainer |
| A new extension or a new contract | a maintainer |

Owners are read from the base branch, never from the pull request, so a pull request can't make its author an owner
and approve itself. Nothing merges unless the checks pass. Every merge that changes an extension's code raises its
version, and its Go module tag (`ext/<name>/vX.Y.Z`) follows that version. A planned extension (a README and no code
yet) stays at `0.0.0`.

```bash
go run ./.github/extensions approvers origin/main HEAD   # who may approve each area a change touches
go run ./.github/extensions versions origin/main HEAD    # every extension whose code changed raised its version
```

## Planned extensions

Our own extensions live in this repo under [`ext/`](../ext), each as its own Go module (`github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/<name>`). See [ext/README.md](../ext/README.md).


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts

# Contracts: how PocketOne fits together

PocketOne is PocketBase plus extensions. What keeps those extensions from turning into a pile of plugins that know
too much about each other is how they meet: through **contracts**.

## The idea

A contract is a promise with a name and a version. `restore/v1` promises one thing: *put this app's data back as it
was at a moment*. It says what you can ask and what you get back. It says nothing about how.

An extension that keeps the promise **provides** the contract. Everything else talks to the contract, never to the
extension behind it: the dashboard, the `pocketone` command, an AI agent over MCP, your `pb_hooks`, and other
extensions.

That's the whole rule: **every API an extension offers is a contract.** Extensions have no private routes and never
import each other.

## An example: restore/v1

Every PocketOne app can restore its data to a moment. Who does the work depends on the app:

| Provider | How close it gets |
|---|---|
| [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr) | Any second in the last three days, from continuous history. |
| [Backups](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/backups), the default | The latest backup made at or before the moment. It steps aside when PITR is on. |
| A multisite host | It could restore an instance from the host's own disk snapshots. |

Asking looks the same whoever answers:

```bash
pocketone remote restore to --at -2h                                   # the command line
curl -X POST https://app.example.com/api/_c/restore/v1/restore \
  -H "Authorization: $TOKEN" -d '{"at": "2026-11-10T15:00:00Z"}'      # HTTP
```

An agent asked to "restore my app to yesterday at 3pm" calls the same operation as an MCP tool. Settings → Backups
shows the contract's own "Restore to a moment" screen. The answer always says which point the data came from: exactly
3pm with PITR, or the 2:00 backup without it.

If something better than PITR comes along tomorrow, it provides `restore/v1`, and nothing that restores apps has to
change.

## Why it matters

- **Swap anything.** Any extension that provides a contract can stand in for another. One line in `pocketone.yaml`
  chooses when several could.
- **Build on anything.** Extensions depend on contracts, not on each other: Deploy requires `remote/v1`, not "the
  Remotes extension". Replace Remotes and Deploy keeps working.
- **One surface, promised.** If a client can call it, it's in a contract: named, versioned, documented and checked.
  Every extension route lives under `/api/_c/<contract id>/`; only paths a standard fixes stay at the root
  (`/.well-known/*`, `/mcp`).
- **Written once, reachable everywhere.** A contract's interface is the source for everything around it. Each
  operation is at once an HTTP endpoint, a `pocketone remote` command, an MCP tool, a hook in Go and in `pb_hooks`,
  and a typed client call. Every one of those paths passes the same checks: superusers only unless the operation is
  public, the token's scopes, and the action hooks.
- **Nothing hidden.** Each app prints who provides what when it starts; `pocketone remote whoami` lists the contracts
  an app offers; the [catalogue](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/all) lists every contract with the extensions that provide it, require it and
  work with it.

## What one interface gives you

Write the interface, run `go generate`, and a contract like `restore/v1` gets all of this:

| Surface | `restore/v1` |
|---|---|
| HTTP API | `GET /api/_c/restore/v1`, `POST /api/_c/restore/v1/restore` |
| Command line | `pocketone remote restore points`, `pocketone remote restore to --at -2h` |
| MCP tools | `restore_points`, `restore_restore_to` |
| Hooks | `restorev1.OnRestoreTo(app, ...)` in Go, `onRestoreRestoreTo(...)` in `pb_hooks` |
| Client | `restorev1.NewClient(url, token, nil).RestoreTo(...)` |
| Dashboard | "Restore to a moment" on Settings → Backups, shown for any provider |

## Who provides what

When an app starts, PocketOne settles every contract and says what it decided:

```
standard: restore/v1 ← pitr (default backups stepped aside)
standard: mail.fallback/v1 ← mailtrap
standard: deploy/v1 ← deploy (default)
```

- **Defaults.** A standard extension often provides a contract as the default: it steps aside as soon as anything
  else provides it.
- **Choices.** When two extensions provide a contract that takes one, the app won't start until `pocketone.yaml`
  picks one:

  ```yaml
  providers:
    restore/v1: pitr
  ```

- **Chains.** Some contracts take several providers in order. Mail with SMTP off goes through `mail.fallback/v1`'s
  chain: the dev inbox in dev mode, then a host's relay.
- **Your own JS.** An app's `pb_hooks` can provide contracts too, in `onContracts((e) => e.provide(...))`.
- **The host.** On a multisite host, some contracts are answered by the host for its instances. An instance running a
  stock PocketBase image in Docker has no PocketOne extensions inside it, but the host still answers `remote/v1` for
  it, so `pocketone remote logs` works there too. The host's own parts are contracts as well: what runs instances
  (`runtime/v1`, Pocker or Docker), what admits requests (`gate/v1`), its TLS (`tls/v1`).

## Versions

A contract's id carries its major version only: `restore/v1`. Within `v1` the promise doesn't change. Changing it
means a `restore/v2` beside `v1`, so whatever relies on `v1` keeps working. A new optional ability is usually a new,
small contract rather than a change to an old one.

## Where contracts live, and who owns them

Every contract, from the standard set or the community, lives in one place: `ext/contracts/<id path>/vN/`
(`mail.fallback/v1` is `ext/contracts/mail/fallback/v1/`). Extensions live in `ext/<name>/`. Keeping contracts
together means one namespace, so two authors can't publish different `rehash/v1`s, and it means one place to look
for what you can build on.

Each contract has a README like an extension's, with its owners and a one-line promise at the top. Its list of the
extensions that provide it, require it and work with it is generated from the code, so it's never out of date.

Whoever first creates a contract owns it. An extension author who needs a contract that doesn't exist yet writes it
first, and then owns both the contract and the extension that provides it. Changes to a contract are reviewed
carefully, because every provider and every caller relies on the promise. Name a contract for what it does
(`restore/v1`), not for the extension that happens to provide it first.

## Words

| Word | Meaning |
|---|---|
| **Contract** | A named, versioned promise: a Go interface plus the API, commands, tools and hooks generated from it. |
| **Provide** | An extension keeps the promise for an app. |
| **Require** | An extension can't work without the contract; without a provider it's turned off, and the startup lines say why. |
| **Works with** | An extension uses the contract when something provides it. |
| **Default** | A provider that steps aside when any other extension provides the contract. |
| **Host-provided** | A multisite host answers the contract for its instances. |

## Next

- [All contracts](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/all): what each one promises, and who provides, requires and works with it.
- [Writing an extension](https://pocketone.dev/docs/writing-an-extension): declare, provide and use contracts in your extension.
- [Add a contract](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/all#add-a-contract): the folder, the README and the generated code.


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/all

# All contracts

New to the idea? Read [How PocketOne fits together](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts) first. This page is the list of every
contract and how to write one.

Every API a PocketOne extension offers is a contract: a versioned Go interface, and the HTTP API, hooks and MCP tools
that come with it, at `/api/_c/<id>/`. Extensions have no routes of their own. An extension says what it
**implements**, **requires** and **works with** in terms of these contracts, never another extension's name, so any
extension that implements a contract can stand in for another. PocketOne answers "who provides this contract on this
app?" at startup and prints the answer.

Every contract lives here, standard or community; extensions live in `ext/<name>`. Each contract is a package named
for its id and major version: `deploy/v1` is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/contracts/deploy/v1`,
`mail.fallback/v1` is `.../mail/fallback/v1`. A change to what a contract promises is a new major version (`v2`) next
to the old one.

The table is generated from each contract's README and every extension's `Contracts()`: run
`go run ./.github/extensions contracts` (CI fails when it's stale).

<!-- contracts:catalogue (generated by `go run ./.github/extensions contracts`; edit each contract's README front matter) -->

| Contract | What it promises | Provided by | Required by | Works with | Owners |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [`bulkmail/v1`](bulkmail/v1/README.md) | Run bulk mail campaigns: count an audience; start, pause, resume, cancel, preview and test a campaign. | bulkmail |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`cli.commands/v1`](cli/commands/v1/README.md) | The pocketone command tree: every contract operation as a remote command by default; extensions replace or add commands. |  |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`deploy/v1`](deploy/v1/README.md) | A project's code files on an app: check, upload, commit, list, read, write, delete, tree. | deploy (default) |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`gate/v1`](gate/v1/README.md) | What admits requests on a multisite host: peer checks, client IPs and rate limits, in order. | firewall |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`http.wrap/v1`](http/wrap/v1/README.md) | Middleware around everything a multisite host serves, nested in order. | servertiming |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`instance.source/v1`](instance/source/v1/README.md) | The instance record a multisite host serves, and where the records come from. | mothership |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`mail.fallback/v1`](mail/fallback/v1/README.md) | Where an app's mail goes when SMTP is off: a chain of providers that send it or pass it on. | mailrelay, mailtrap |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`mail.feedback/v1`](mail/feedback/v1/README.md) | Mail providers' reports (bounces, complaints, unsubscribes) received at one place and raised as events any extension can act on. | bulkmail (default) |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`mail.suppression/v1`](mail/suppression/v1/README.md) | Addresses an app must not send bulk mail to, and the unsubscribe link every bulk message carries. | bulkmail (default) |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`mcp/v1`](mcp/v1/README.md) | The app's MCP endpoint at /mcp, with every provided contract's operations as tools. | mcp (default) |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`oauth/v1`](oauth/v1/README.md) | The app's OAuth 2.1 authorization server, so the CLI and MCP clients can sign in. | tokens |  | mcp | @benallfree |
| [`remote/v1`](remote/v1/README.md) | Remote control of an app: whoami, status, restart, logs. The base every client starts from. | docker, remotes (default) | deploy |  | @benallfree |
| [`restore/v1`](restore/v1/README.md) | Put an app's data back as it was at a moment: from continuous history, or the latest backup before it. | backups (default), pitr |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`runtime/v1`](runtime/v1/README.md) | What runs a multisite host's instances (in-process, in containers), in preference order. | docker, pocker |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`settings/v1`](settings/v1/README.md) | The settings an app's admins change for its extensions, one API for all of them. | settings (default) |  | bulkmail, mailrelay, pitr | @benallfree |
| [`tls/v1`](tls/v1/README.md) | The TLS of a multisite host's listener: automatic certificates instead of certificate files. | autotls |  |  | @benallfree |
| [`tokens/v1`](tokens/v1/README.md) | An app's API tokens: check one, register scopes, read a request's token, limit in-process requests; the token API. | tokens |  | deploy, mcp, remotes | @benallfree |

<!-- /contracts:catalogue -->

[`internal/example/v1`](internal/example/v1/example.go) is a test-only wire contract that exercises the generated code.

## Three kinds

- **Service:** a Go interface, looked up in the same process (`fallbackv1.Contract.Of(app)`).
- **Wire:** a service with an HTTP API under `/api/_c/<id>/`, generated from its interface: each method is an
  operation with its own HTTP method, path and token scope (`//op: POST restart scope=remote`); inputs and results are
  JSON, uploads (`extkit.RawIn`), downloads (`extkit.RawOut`) or streams (`extkit.Stream`, sent as server-sent
  events). It gets action hooks (`remotev1.OnRestart`, `onRemoteRestart` in `pb_hooks`), an MCP tool per JSON
  operation and a client. Every caller (HTTP, MCP, Go) passes the same scope check and hooks.
- **Routed:** a contract whose provider is an `http.Handler` serving everything under `/api/_c/<id>/` as it is, for an
  API a protocol shapes (OAuth) or an existing API moved under a contract (deploy/v1).

A multisite host can provide a wire or routed contract for its instances, so it works for instances that run stock
PocketBase.

A contract can bring its own dashboard screen (`Contract.UI(name, fsys)`): it shows on every app that provides the
contract, whichever extension does, and calls only the contract's API. restore/v1's "Restore to a moment" works this
way.

An extension that calls a contract for its own work (bulk mail checking whoever keeps the suppression list) passes
`extkit.Internal` as the auth, and can ask who provides it with `Contract.Provider(app)`.

## Add a contract

A contract is a folder `ext/contracts/<id path>/vN/` (`mail.fallback/v1` → `mail/fallback/v1/`) with:

- the Go package: the interface, its `//contract:` directives and `zz_contract.go`;
- a `README.md`, its page on pocketone.dev, with front matter and four sections in this order:

  ```markdown
  ---
  owners: ["@your-github-handle"]
  summary: "One line: what the contract promises."
  ---

  # mail.fallback/v1

  ## Use        how to call it: HTTP, Go, pb_hooks, MCP, CLI
  ## Provide    how to implement it
  ## Extensions (generated: who provides, requires and works with it)
  ## License    MIT
  ```

Whoever first creates a contract owns it; an extension author who adds one owns both the contract and the extension
that provides it. Ids are unique across PocketOne. Pick a name for what the contract does (`restore/v1`), not for the
extension that first provides it.

## Write the interface

A contract is an interface with `//contract:` directives; [`contractgen`](cmd/contractgen/main.go) writes the rest
(`zz_contract.go`) with `go generate ./...`. A test fails when a generated file is stale.

```go
//go:generate go run github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/contracts/cmd/contractgen

// Deployer sends a project's code to an app.
//
//contract:id deploy/v1
//contract:kind wire
//contract:scope deploy
//contract:host
//contract:js hooks
type Deployer interface {
	// Upload writes changed files to the app.
	Upload(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, in UploadInput) (UploadResult, error)
}
```

Methods take `ctx`, then (wire) `extkit.Auth`, then at most one input; they return `error` or one value and `error`.
The doc comment of a wire method is its MCP tool's description. Contracts are reviewed like PocketOne's core: a
contract is a promise every implementation keeps.

## Use one

```go
// provide (in Register)
deployv1.Contract.ProvideDefault(app, myDeployer{})

// consume (after registration: in hooks, at serve time)
d := deployv1.Contract.Must(app)

// declare it, so PocketOne can order and switch extensions
func (e *Extension) Contracts() extkit.Contracts {
	return extkit.Contracts{Implements: extkit.IDs("deploy/v1"), Defaults: extkit.IDs("deploy/v1")}
}
```

Choose between providers in `pocketone.yaml`:

```yaml
providers:
  mail.fallback/v1: mailrelay
```

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/bulkmail/v1

# bulkmail/v1

Campaigns to many recipients, sent at a pace the app's mail account can take. Campaigns are records in the
provider's collection, created and edited with PocketBase's records API; this contract runs them. The list of
addresses never to mail is [mail.suppression/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.suppression/v1); providers' bounce and
complaint reports are [mail.feedback/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.feedback/v1).

A wire contract ([bulkmail.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/bulkmail/v1/bulkmail.go)).

## Use

| Operation | HTTP (`POST`) | Body | Token scope |
|---|---|---|---|
| Count | `/api/_c/bulkmail/v1/count` | `{"audience": {...}}` | `bulkmail:read` |
| Start | `/api/_c/bulkmail/v1/start` | `{"campaign": "<id>", "limit": 0}` | `bulkmail` |
| Pause, Resume, Cancel | `/api/_c/bulkmail/v1/pause` (`resume`, `cancel`) | `{"campaign": "<id>"}` | `bulkmail` |
| Preview | `/api/_c/bulkmail/v1/preview` | `{"campaign": "<id>", "email": ""}` | `bulkmail:read` |
| Test | `/api/_c/bulkmail/v1/test` | `{"campaign": "<id>", "to": ""}` | `bulkmail` |

Campaign actions answer `{"campaign": <the record>}`. The audience's shape is the provider's (see
[Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail)). Only superusers may call these. Agents get them as MCP tools
(`bulkmail_start`, ...); `pb_hooks` can hook each (`onBulkmailStart`).

## Provide

Implement `bulkmailv1.Campaigns` and provide it in your extension's `Register`.

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cli.commands/v1

# cli.commands/v1

The `pocketone` command tree. Every operation of every wire contract linked into the binary is a command under
`remote`, with no code: `pocketone remote restore to --at -2h` calls restore/v1's `RestoreTo` on the project's
remote. An extension replaces one of those commands by providing the same path, or adds commands of its own. One
provider per path; when two extensions provide the same path, `pocketone.yaml` picks one.

A keyed contract (by command path), in the developer's `pocketone` process ([commands.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/cli/commands/v1/commands.go)).

## Use

The generated commands, for any contract:

- **Path:** `remote`, the contract id's words, then the operation: restore/v1's `restore_to` is
  `remote restore to`, mail.suppression/v1's `check` is `remote mail suppression check`, remote/v1's `status` is
  `remote status` (`clicmdv1.PathOf`).
- **Flags:** one per field of the operation's input (`--at`, `--email`, `--campaign`), plus `--json` for the
  whole input (`@file`, `-` for stdin) and `--remote` (a remote's name or a URL; default: the project's default
  remote). Times take RFC 3339, a local time (`2026-11-10 15:00`) or a duration from now (`-2h`).
- **Output:** the answer as JSON; streams print one JSON line per entry until Ctrl-C.
- **Auth:** the remote's saved login (`pocketone login`), or `P1_TOKEN` in CI.
- **Not commands:** public operations that take or return a raw body (an unsubscribe page, a mail provider's
  webhook); they're for browsers and services.

A remote that doesn't offer the contract answers "this remote doesn't offer restore/v1".

## Provide

Provide a command in your extension's `Register`. The same path as a generated command replaces it; a new path adds
one:

```go
clicmdv1.Contract.Provide(app, clicmdv1.Command{
	Path:  "remote rehash",
	Short: "Rehash every stored password",
	Flags: func(fs *pflag.FlagSet) { fs.Bool("dry-run", false, "only count") },
	Run: func(c *clicmdv1.Ctx, args []string) error {
		caller, err := c.Caller("rehash/v1") // the command's remote, with its login
		if err != nil {
			return err
		}
		return caller.Call(c, "POST", "", nil, nil)
	},
})
```

and declare `Implements: extkit.IDs("cli.commands/v1")`. Two providers of one path fail the start until
`pocketone.yaml` picks:

```yaml
providers:
  cli.commands/v1:
    remote rehash: rehasher
```

A binary builds its tree with `clicmdv1.Mount(app, rootCmd)` once the app's contracts are sealed; the standard set
does it in `Register`. Commands already on the tree (`remote add`, `remote whoami`) stay unless a provider replaces
them.

## Extensions

# deploy/v1

A project's code on an app: `pb_hooks`, `pb_migrations`, `pb_public` and packages. Clients send only the files
the app lacks, then swap the new set in at once. Restart and logs are [remote/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1)'s, which
it requires.

A routed contract ([deploy.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/deploy/v1/deploy.go)): its provider is an `http.Handler` serving the file API below. A
multisite host can provide it for its instances.

## Use

| HTTP | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /api/_c/deploy/v1/check` | which files the app lacks (JSON) |
| `POST /api/_c/deploy/v1/blobs` | upload them (gzip bytes) |
| `POST /api/_c/deploy/v1/commit` | swap the new code set in (JSON) |
| `GET /api/_c/deploy/v1/files` | list deployed files |
| `DELETE /api/_c/deploy/v1/files` | delete files |
| `GET` / `PUT /api/_c/deploy/v1/files/raw` | read or write one file (raw bytes) |
| `GET /api/_c/deploy/v1/tree` | the app's code tree, for two-way sync |

Token scopes: `deploy` (everything) and `deploy:read` (list, read, tree). The CLI: `pocketone deploy`, `dev`,
`pull`.

## Provide

Provide an `http.Handler` that serves the API under `deployv1.Prefix`:

```go
deployv1.Contract.ProvideDefault(app, handler)
```

A host provides it for its instances with `deployv1.Contract.ProvideForInstances(host, factory)` and
`extkit.HostRoutes(host, deployv1.Contract, multisite.InstanceID, next)` in its instance routes
(`multisite.Host.InstanceRoutes`, after the gates).

# gate/v1

What admits requests on a multisite host before an instance is served here or forwarded to another server: a peer
allow list, the real client IP behind a proxy, rate limits. Gates run in order and every one must admit; a gate may
answer the request itself (429, 403).

A host-scope service contract, many providers in order ([gate.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/gate/v1/gate.go)).

## Use

Nothing to call: the host runs every gate on every request. Pick or order them in `pocketone.yaml`:

```yaml
providers:
  gate/v1: [firewall]
```

## Provide

Implement `gatev1.Gate` (`AllowPeer` before routing, `Admit` per instance, returning a release function), and
`gatev1.ClientIPResolver` if the gate knows the real client. Provide it in a host extension's `RegisterHost`:

```go
gatev1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, myGate)
```

|---|---|

# http.wrap/v1

Middleware around everything a multisite host serves: health, every instance, forwarded requests. Wrappers nest in
provider order, the first outermost (a Server-Timing header first, so it measures everything inside it).

A host-scope service contract, many providers in order ([wrap.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/http/wrap/v1/wrap.go)).

## Use

Nothing to call: the host wraps its handler with every provider. Order them in `pocketone.yaml` if needed:

```yaml
providers:
  http.wrap/v1: [servertiming]
```

## Provide

Implement `wrapv1.Wrapper` (`Wrap(next http.Handler) http.Handler`) and provide it in a host extension's
`RegisterHost`:

```go
wrapv1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, myWrapper)
```

# instance.source/v1

The record of one instance on a multisite host: its id, hostnames, PocketBase version, folder, secrets, limits,
superusers, per-extension settings, whether it's blocked or runs elsewhere. Every host contract reads the same record:
runtimes run it, gates admit requests for it. A source supplies the records and streams changes.

A host-scope service contract ([instance.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/instance/source/v1/instance.go), [limits.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/instance/source/v1/limits.go)).

## Use

A host takes its records from whichever extension provides this contract: by default its `instances` file
(`instances: { file: instances.yaml }`), or a control plane's mirror (ext/mothership). In Go the record is
`sourcev1.Instance` (`multisite.Instance` is the same type).

## Provide

Implement `sourcev1.Source`: `Snapshot(ctx)` returns every instance, `Watch(ctx)` streams changes (upserts and
deletes) until ctx is done. Provide it on the host's scope in a host extension's `RegisterHost`:

```go
sourcev1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, mySource)
```

# mail.fallback/v1

Where an app's mail goes when its SMTP is off. Providers form an ordered chain: each sends a message or passes it on;
when all pass, PocketBase sends it its own way (`sendmail`). An app with SMTP on never reaches the chain.

A service ([fallback.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/mail/fallback/v1/fallback.go)), many providers, open to `pb_hooks`.

## Use

Nothing to call: mail an app sends with SMTP off goes through the chain. Order the providers in `pocketone.yaml`:

```yaml
providers:
  mail.fallback/v1: [mailtrap, mailrelay]
```

## Provide

Implement `fallbackv1.Sender` (`Send(ctx, *mailer.Message)`, returning `fallbackv1.ErrPass` to pass), provide it,
and bind the chain once:

```go
fallbackv1.Contract.Provide(app, mySender{})
fallbackv1.Bind(app)
```

From `pb_hooks`:

```js
onContracts((e) => {
  e.provide("mail.fallback/v1", {
    send(m) {
      if (!m.to.some((a) => a.address.endsWith("@example.com"))) throw new ContractError("pass")
      // send it your way
    },
  })
  e.next()
})
```

## Extensions

| Extension | |
|---|---|
| [mailrelay](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailrelay) | provides |
| [mailtrap](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailtrap) | provides |

<!-- /contracts:index -->

# mail.feedback/v1

What mail providers report back about mail an app sent: bounces, spam complaints, unsubscribes. The provider of this
contract receives the reports and raises one event per address; any number of extensions act on them through one
hook. A suppression list adds the address, a CRM marks the contact, `pb_hooks` logs it.

A wire contract ([feedback.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/mail/feedback/v1/feedback.go)). Its operations are public: SES messages are checked by their SNS
signature, webhook calls by a shared secret.

## Use

| Operation | HTTP | What sends it |
|---|---|---|
| SES | `POST /api/_c/mail.feedback/v1/ses` | an Amazon SNS HTTPS subscription for SES bounce and complaint notifications |
| Webhook | `POST /api/_c/mail.feedback/v1/webhook` with `X-Feedback-Secret` | any provider: `{"type": "bounce\|complaint\|unsubscribe", "email": "...", "campaign": "..."}` |

Act on the events in Go:

```go
feedbackv1.OnEvent(app).BindFunc(func(e *feedbackv1.Event) error {
	// e.Kind: bounce, complaint or unsubscribe; e.Email, e.Campaign, e.Source
	return e.Next()
})
```

## Provide

Implement `feedbackv1.Receiver`: check each report, then call `feedbackv1.Raise(app, &feedbackv1.Event{...})` for
each address. Where the webhook secret comes from is the provider's (Bulk Mail keeps it in its settings).

## Extensions

| Extension | |
|---|---|
| [bulkmail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail) | provides (default) |

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mail.suppression/v1

# mail.suppression/v1

The addresses an app must not send bulk mail to (unsubscribed, bounced, complained, added by hand), and the
unsubscribe link in every bulk message. Anything that mails many people checks it.

A wire contract ([suppression.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/mail/suppression/v1/suppression.go)).

## Use

| Operation | HTTP | Who |
|---|---|---|
| Check | `GET /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/check?email=` | superusers (`suppression:read`) |
| Suppress | `POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/suppress` `{"email", "reason", "source", "campaign"}` | superusers (`suppression`) |
| Unsuppress | `POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsuppress` `{"email"}` | superusers (`suppression`) |
| UnsubscribePage | `GET /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsubscribe?t=<signed token>` | public: the link in a message |
| Unsubscribe | `POST /api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsubscribe` | public: the page's form, or a mail provider's one-click POST |

Reasons: `unsubscribed`, `bounced`, `complained`, `manual`. The page never unsubscribes on a `GET` (link scanners
open every URL in a message); one-click unsubscribes follow RFC 8058 (`List-Unsubscribe=One-Click`). The token is
signed by the provider, so only links it issued work.

## Provide

Implement `suppressionv1.List`; sign the tokens in the links your messages carry, and point `List-Unsubscribe`
at `/api/_c/mail.suppression/v1/unsubscribe?t=...`.

## Extensions

| Extension | |
|---|---|
| [bulkmail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail) | provides (default) |

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/mcp/v1

# mcp/v1

The app's [Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io) endpoint, so agents (a Claude connector, Claude
Code, any Streamable HTTP client) can work with it. It stays at `/mcp`: people paste that URL, MCP versions itself
in the protocol, and OAuth tokens are bound to the resource URL.

What every provider serves the same way, the contract owns:

- **The routes:** `/mcp`, and its protected resource metadata at `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp`.
- **The tools:** every wire contract the app provides, one tool per operation (`restore_points`, `bulkmail_start`,
  ...), with an input schema from the operation's types and called through the contract, so the same superuser
  check, scopes and hooks apply as over HTTP; and tools extensions add with `AddTool`.

A provider brings the protocol, sign-in and any tools of its own ([MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) adds `pb_*` tools over
the REST API). Replace it and the contract tools stay.

A service ([mcp.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/mcp/v1/mcp.go)).

## Use

Add `https://<host>/mcp` to an MCP client and sign in. In Go, an extension adds a tool that isn't a contract
operation, and tells agents what its tools are for:

```go
mcpv1.AddTool(app, mcpv1.Tool{
	Name:        "notes_summarize_week",
	Description: "Summarizes this week's notes.",
	ReadOnly:    true,
	Call: func(ctx context.Context, a extkit.Auth, args json.RawMessage) (any, error) { ... },
})
mcpv1.AddInstructions(app, "Use notes_summarize_week for weekly reviews.")
```

`mcpv1.Tools(app)` lists what every provider serves.

## Provide

Implement `mcpv1.Endpoint` (`ServeMCP` for requests to `/mcp`, `Metadata` for the protected resource metadata),
provide it, and bind the routes once:

```go
mcpv1.Contract.ProvideDefault(app, myServer{})
mcpv1.Bind(app)
```

Serve `mcpv1.Tools(app)` in `tools/list` and `tools/call`, calling each tool as the signed-in caller.

`/mcp` skips PocketBase's `pbRejectUnknownToken`, so the provider rejects a bad token itself: a request with an
`Authorization` header and no signed-in caller (`e.Auth` is nil) gets 401 with a `WWW-Authenticate: Bearer
error="invalid_token"` challenge, never a guest's answer.

## Extensions

<!-- contracts:index (generated by `go run ./.github/extensions contracts` from each extension's Contracts(); don't edit) -->

| Extension | |
|---|---|
| [mcp](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) | provides (default) |

<!-- /contracts:index -->

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/oauth/v1

# oauth/v1

An OAuth 2.1 authorization server for the app: authorization code with PKCE, device code, refresh, revocation, and
client registration (dynamic, or by a client metadata document). The CLI's browser login and MCP clients such as
Claude sign in through it, and get API tokens ([tokens/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/tokens/v1)).

A routed contract ([oauth.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/oauth/v1/oauth.go)): the OAuth specs fix its API's shape, so its provider serves it as it is.

## Use

| HTTP | What it does |
|---|---|
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` | the server's metadata (RFC 8414 puts it at the root) |
| `GET` / `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/authorize` | sign in and consent (browser) |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/token` | codes and refresh tokens for access tokens |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/device` | start a device-code sign-in |
| `GET` / `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/device/verify` | enter the device code (browser) |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/revoke` | revoke a token |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/register` | dynamic client registration (when on) |
| `GET` / `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/provider/callback` | sign-in through an OAuth2 provider (Google, Apple, ...) |

In Go, another extension (MCP) turns on dynamic registration and sets token lifetimes:
`oauthv1.Contract.Of(app)` → `EnableDynamicRegistration()`, `SetAccessTTL(path, ttl)`, `Issuer(e)`.

## Provide

Implement `oauthv1.Server` and serve the routes above (`extkit.EventServer` or `extkit.RouteBinder`); issue access
tokens through tokens/v1.

## Extensions

<!-- contracts:index (generated by `go run ./.github/extensions contracts` from each extension's Contracts(); don't edit) -->

| Extension | |
|---|---|
| [tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) | provides |
| [mcp](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) | works with |

<!-- /contracts:index -->

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/remote/v1

# remote/v1

Remote control of an app from afar: who your credential is and what the app offers, its status, a restart, and its
log. Every client starts here: `GET /api/_c/remote/v1` is the one fixed path, and its answer lists every other
contract the app offers. Contracts that add an area (deploy/v1) require this one.

A wire contract ([remote.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/remote/v1/remote.go)); a multisite host can provide it for its instances, so it works for
instances running stock PocketBase images.

## Use

| Operation | HTTP | Token scope |
|---|---|---|
| Whoami | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1` | public (the answer says more when you're signed in) |
| Status | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/status` | `remote:read` |
| Restart | `POST /api/_c/remote/v1/restart` | `remote` |
| Logs | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/logs?n=100` (server-sent events) | `remote:read` |

- **CLI:** `pocketone remote whoami | status | restart | logs`.
- **Go:** `remotev1.Contract.Must(app)` in the app, or `remotev1.NewClient(url, token, http)` from outside. The
  command-line client (linked remotes, saved logins, sign-in) is [remoteclient](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient).
- **Hooks:** `remotev1.OnRestart(app)` in Go, `onRemoteRestart` in `pb_hooks`, for every operation.
- **MCP:** a tool per operation (`remote_status`, ...).

## Provide

Implement `remotev1.Remote` and provide it in your extension's `Register`:

```go
remotev1.Contract.Provide(app, myRemote{})
```

A multisite host provides it for every instance with `remotev1.Contract.ProvideForInstances(host, factory)` and
serves it with `remotev1.W.HostHandler` in its instance routes (`multisite.Host.InstanceRoutes`, after the gates;
see [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) and
[docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker)).

## Extensions

<!-- contracts:index (generated by `go run ./.github/extensions contracts` from each extension's Contracts(); don't edit) -->

| Extension | |
|---|---|
| [docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) | provides |
| [remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes) | provides (default) |
| [deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | requires |

<!-- /contracts:index -->

## License

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/restore/v1

# restore/v1

Put an app's data back as it was at a moment. You ask for a moment ("Tuesday 15:00"); the app restores the closest
point it has at or before it and tells you which one it used. Providers differ only in how close they get:

- [pitr](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr) keeps continuous history: any second inside its window.
- [backups](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/backups), the default, uses PocketBase's own backups (local or S3): the latest backup
  made at or before the moment. It steps aside when pitr is on for the app.

The app restarts to apply a restore; its data from before the restore is kept until the next one.

A wire contract ([restore.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/restore/v1/restore.go)); a multisite host may provide it for its instances (from host-level
snapshots).

## Use

| Operation | HTTP | Token scope |
|---|---|---|
| Points: what can be restored | `GET /api/_c/restore/v1` | `restore:read` |
| RestoreTo a moment | `POST /api/_c/restore/v1/restore` with `{"at": "<RFC 3339 time>"}` | `restore` |

`Points` answers with the provider's name and either a `window` (`kind: "continuous"`) or a list of `snapshots`
(`kind: "snapshots"`, newest first), whether a restore is running, and the last restore. `RestoreTo` answers with
the `point` it restores from; `422 no_point` when there's nothing at or before the moment, `409 busy` while another
restore runs. Only superusers may call either.

- **Dashboard:** Settings → Backups gets a "Restore to a moment" section from this contract ([ui/main.js](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/restore/v1/ui/main.js)),
  whichever extension provides it: a time picker over pitr's window, or one that says which backup a moment uses.
- **Go:** `restorev1.Contract.Must(app).RestoreTo(ctx, auth, restorev1.RestoreInput{At: t})`, or
  `restorev1.NewClient(url, token, http)` from outside.
- **Hooks:** `restorev1.OnRestoreTo(app, fn)` in Go, `onRestoreRestoreTo` in `pb_hooks`: refuse or log a restore.
- **MCP:** `restore_points` and `restore_restore_to`.

## Provide

Implement `restorev1.Restorer` and provide it in your extension's `Register` (`ProvideDefault` if a better
provider should replace yours). Report the point you'll actually restore from, and restart the app to apply it.

## Extensions

<!-- contracts:index (generated by `go run ./.github/extensions contracts` from each extension's Contracts(); don't edit) -->

| Extension | |
|---|---|
| [pitr](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr) | provides |
| [backups](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/backups) | provides (default) |

<!-- /contracts:index -->

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/runtime/v1

# runtime/v1

What runs a multisite host's instances: [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) in-process,
[docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) in containers. A host can have several at once, in preference order: each
instance runs on the one it names (`runtime: docker` in its record), else the first that can serve it (by PocketBase
version, for example). Having a `multisite` section makes the binary a host; the runtimes are this contract's
providers.

A host-scope service contract, many providers in order ([runtime.go](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/runtime/v1/runtime.go)).

## Use

Pick and order the runtimes in `pocketone.yaml`; by default it's every linked runtime that's configured, in link
order (docker needs its `docker` section):

```yaml
multisite: {}
providers:
  runtime/v1: [pocker, docker]   # pocker first; docker for what pocker can't serve
```

## Provide

Implement `runtimev1.Runtime` (`Name`, `Serves`, `ServeInstance`, `Ready`) and any optional hooks the host
calls (`Prechecker`, `Syncer`, `Starter`, `Shutdowner`, `Statser`). Provide it in a host extension's
`RegisterHost`, only when it's configured:

```go
runtimev1.Contract.ProvideIn(h.Scope, myRuntime)
```

## Extensions

<!-- contracts:index (generated by `go run ./.github/extensions contracts` from each extension's Contracts(); don't edit) -->

| Extension | |
|---|---|
| [docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) | provides |
| [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | provides |

<!-- /contracts:index -->
