# S3 Redirect

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

File downloads as short-lived signed redirects to your bucket, after PocketBase's own access check.

When an app keeps its files in S3 (Settings → Files storage), PocketBase normally downloads each file from the bucket
and streams it to the browser. With S3 Redirect, `/api/files/...` answers **302** with a presigned GET URL instead,
and the browser fetches the file straight from the bucket. The app's bandwidth, memory and connections stay free.
With Cloudflare R2 the downloads cost no egress either.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

S3 Redirect is built into `pocketone` and **on by default**. It only acts when S3 file storage is on: turn on S3 in
Settings → Files storage and downloads redirect. With files on local disk, nothing changes.

To stream files through the app as before:

```bash
pocketone serve --s3Redirect=false
```

In your own Go build, register it before the app starts:

```go
import "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/s3redirect"

app := pocketbase.New()
s3redirect.MustRegister(app, s3redirect.Config{TTL: 5 * time.Minute})
app.Start()
```

Then turn on S3 in Settings → Files storage.

## Configure

Set it in `pocketone.yaml`:

```yaml
s3redirect:
  enabled: true   # false streams files through the app
  ttl: 5m         # how long each signed URL is valid
```

Or with flags, which win over the file:

| Flag | Default | What it does |
|---|---|---|
| `--s3Redirect` | `true` | Redirect downloads when S3 file storage is on. `--s3Redirect=false` streams them. |
| `--s3RedirectTTL` | `5m` | How long each signed URL stays valid (at most 7 days). |

Keep the TTL short: anyone holding a URL can fetch the file until it expires, protected files included.

The bucket itself is PocketBase's own S3 setting, in **Settings → Files storage**. There are no other settings
screens.

**Bucket CORS.** A redirect followed by `fetch()` or `<img crossorigin>` from your site needs a CORS rule on the
bucket allowing `GET` from your origin. Plain `<img>`, `<video>` and links need nothing.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `s3redirect:`

Signed S3 redirects for file downloads: enabled, URL lifetime. The --s3Redirect and --s3RedirectTTL flags win.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `enabled` | bool |  | On unless false (it only acts when S3 file storage is on). Flag: --s3Redirect. |
| `ttl` | duration |  | How long each signed URL stays valid. Default 5m, max 7 days. Flag: --s3RedirectTTL. |

## Use

Once S3 is on, there's nothing to click. File URLs stay the same; they answer with a redirect:

- **Access checks don't change.** PocketBase still finds the record, checks protected-file tokens and the view rule,
  and creates thumbnails on first request. The redirect happens only after all of that.
- **The file token stays private.** It never goes into the bucket URL, and the redirect sends
  `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
- **Same headers as PocketBase:** inline or attachment (`?download=1`), the filename, and forced content types (SVG,
  CSS, JS) are signed into the URL as S3 `response-*` overrides. Range requests work, because S3 serves them.
- **Caching:** the browser may reuse the redirect for 80% of the TTL (`Cache-Control: private`, never shared
  caches); the file itself gets PocketBase's usual 30-day `Cache-Control`.
- **Falls back to streaming** when S3 is off, the extension is turned off, or signing fails. A failed signature logs a
  warning, `s3redirect: signing failed, streaming instead`.
- Only `GET` and `HEAD` requests are redirected.

**Inline vs attachment:** PocketBase decides this from the stored content type; S3 Redirect goes by the file
extension (it doesn't ask the bucket, so a redirect costs no extra round trip). They agree for every file PocketBase
names.

### Try it

```
cd example && go run . serve
```

The example runs one app with its own in-process bucket, nothing to set up. It:

- starts an S3-compatible bucket on `127.0.0.1:9199` ([gofakes3](https://github.com/johannesboyne/gofakes3),
  objects kept in `pb_data/demo-s3.bolt`), and points the app's Files storage at it;
- seeds a `demo_files` record with an image (thumbs `100x100`) and a protected text file, uploaded through PocketBase;
- prints the URLs to open. Each answers `302` to the bucket.

The bucket only serves presigned GETs whose signature, re-computed with the **AWS SDK's own SigV4 signer**, matches
and hasn't expired, and logs each one (`demo bucket: presigned GET ..., signature valid`). Unsigned or edited URLs get
`403`. So a working download proves the signatures are AWS-compatible, not just accepted by a lenient fake.

`S3REDIRECT_DEMO=0` skips the demo bucket (use your own Files storage settings); `S3REDIRECT_DEMO_ADDR` moves it.
The example is its own Go module, so its demo dependencies (gofakes3, the AWS SDK signer) never reach the extension's
`go.mod`.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | The same extension runs on every instance. The `s3redirect` section sets the defaults; each instance can override `enabled` and `ttl` (below). |
| [S3 Fallback](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3-fallback) | Apps without their own S3 settings keep files in its bucket (under pocker, fenced to `instances/<id>/storage/`). Its driver signs, so those downloads redirect too. |

### Per-instance settings (pocker)

```go
srv.Extensions = append(srv.Extensions, s3redirect.New(s3redirect.Config{}))
```

```yaml
s3redirect:            # server defaults
  enabled: true        # on unless false
  ttl: 5m

instances:
  - id: abc
    extensions:
      s3redirect: { enabled: false }   # per instance: enabled, ttl
```

It's an [extkit](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/extkit/extkit.go) extension, so the same value works on a single app and on every pocker
instance; it doesn't link pocker.

### Building on S3 Redirect

- **Supply your own bucket.** S3 Redirect signs for whatever filesystem PocketBase serves the download from: the
  app's own S3 settings, or one an extension supplies through `OnFilesystemCreate`. Implement `s3redirect.Signer`
  (`SignedURL(key, ttl, now, overrides)`) on your filesystem driver and its downloads redirect. Nothing else needs
  wiring; a filesystem that can't sign (local disk) streams as usual.
- **Your own download handlers run first.** The extension binds `OnFileDownloadRequest` last (priority 1000, id
  `s3redirect.HookID`, `__ext_s3redirect__`), so your Go or JS handlers can still change the served file or answer
  themselves without calling `e.Next()`. Unbind the id to turn it off for one app.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](example/main.go) starts its own in-process S3 bucket, points the app's file storage at it and seeds a record, so every download redirect works with nothing to set up. Run `go run . serve` in `example/` and open the URLs it prints.

```go
// Command example runs one PocketOne app whose file downloads redirect to an S3 bucket, with nothing to set up:
// it starts its own S3-compatible bucket in-process (gofakes3, stored in pb_data/demo-s3.bolt), points the app's
// Files storage at it, and seeds a "demo_files" record with an image and a protected document.
//
//	go run . serve
//
// Open the URLs it prints. Each answers 302 with a signed URL; the bucket logs every fetch and only serves it if the
// signature is valid and unexpired, checked independently with the AWS SDK's SigV4 signer.
//
// Set S3REDIRECT_DEMO=0 to skip the demo bucket and use whatever Files storage you configure in the dashboard.
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"log"
	"os"
	"time"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/s3redirect"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"

	s3redirect.MustRegister(app, s3redirect.Config{TTL: 5 * time.Minute})

	if os.Getenv("S3REDIRECT_DEMO") != "0" {
		addr := os.Getenv("S3REDIRECT_DEMO_ADDR")
		if addr == "" {
			addr = "127.0.0.1:9199"
		}
		registerDemo(app, addr)
	}

	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## How it works

- Go module `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/s3redirect`, no dependencies beyond PocketOne.
- The redirect is an `OnFileDownloadRequest` handler; the hook already exists upstream, so there's no core change.
- Signing is SigV4 query-string auth in [`sigv4`](sigv4/sigv4.go), checked against AWS's documented example. It needs
  no change to PocketBase's S3 client. The TTL is clamped to between 1 second and 7 days.

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens

# Tokens

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Long-lived API tokens for your app: secrets that start with `pbt_`, for CI, deploys, scripts and agents. Each token
belongs to an account and acts as that account. It can be limited to scopes, given an expiry, and revoked on its own.
Send one as `Authorization: Bearer pbt_…`. Ordinary PocketBase auth tokens keep working unchanged.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Tokens is built into `pocketone` and always on. There's nothing to install or turn on.

In your own Go build, register it before the app starts:

```go
app := pocketbase.New()
tokens.MustRegister(app, tokens.Config{})
app.Start()
```

To use `$tokens` in `pb_hooks`, bind it in jsvm's `OnInit` (the stock binary does):

```go
jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{OnInit: func(rt js.Runtime) { tokens.BindJS(app, rt) }})
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/tokens`.

## Configure

There is no `pocketone.yaml` section, flag or environment variable for Tokens. In `pocketone`:
- any account (a superuser, or a record of any auth collection) can own tokens;
- a token never expires unless you give it an expiry.

A Go build can narrow both (see [Go config](#go-config)).

### Scopes

A token without scopes has its owner's full rights. A token with scopes works only on the requests its scopes cover,
plus remote/v1's whoami (`/api/_c/remote/v1`); anywhere else it gets `403`. Extensions and your own `pb_hooks` register the scopes. In
`pocketone` the built-in ones are:

| Scope | From | Allows | Who can hold it |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deploy` | [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | Deploy code (hooks, migrations, public files, packages), read files and logs | superusers |
| `deploy:read` | [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | Read deployed files and stream logs | superusers |

`pocketone token scopes` lists every scope your app has, with its paths.

### Your own scopes

Declare a scope at the top level of a `pb_hooks` file. It then shows up in **Settings → API tokens** and on the
[the OAuth server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth) consent page:

```js
// pb_hooks/scopes.pb.js
$tokens.registerScope({
  name: 'notes:read',                        // lower-case letters, digits, ":" and "_"
  description: 'Read notes',                 // shown in the token screen and on the consent page
  paths: ['/api/collections/notes/records'], // URL prefixes where a token holding it works
  methods: ['GET'],                          // optional: only these methods (GET covers HEAD)
})
$tokens.registerScope({ name: 'notes:write', description: 'Change notes', paths: ['/api/collections/notes/records'] })
```

- `collections: ['users']` limits which accounts may hold the scope.
- Registering a name again merges its paths, methods and collections, so reloading hooks is safe.
- Two names whose headers would be the same (`notes:write` and `notes_write`) can't both be registered.

Check a scope on your own route:

```js
routerAdd('POST', '/api/notes/archive', (e) => { /* ... */ }, $apis.requireAuth(), $tokens.requireScope('notes:write'))
```

`$tokens.requireScope` refuses a signed-out request, and a token that doesn't hold the scope. Inside a handler,
`$tokens.hasScope(e, 'notes:write')` tells you the same.

Check a scope in a collection API rule. Every signed-in request carries `X-Token-Scope-<Name>: 1` for each scope it
holds, and rules read it as `@request.headers.x_token_scope_<name>` (`:` becomes `_`):

```
@request.auth.id = owner && @request.headers.x_token_scope_notes_write = "1"
```

- A PocketBase auth token or an unscoped API token holds every registered scope (except ones its collection can't
  hold).
- A scoped token holds only its own scopes. A signed-out request holds none.
- Headers a client sends with that prefix are always dropped, so they can't be forged.

`$tokens.ruleField('notes:write')` returns the rule field for a name, and `$tokens.scopes()` lists every registered
scope with its header and rule field.

## Use

### From the dashboard

1. Open **Settings → API tokens** (under **Access**). Only superusers see this screen.
2. Fill in a **Name**. Optionally set **Expires in (days)**, and tick any **Scopes** (none means full rights).
3. By default the token is yours. To make one for another account, fill in **Owner collection** (default
   `_superusers`) and **Owner (id or email)**.
4. Click **Create token**. Copy the token now: it's shown only once and never stored.

The list shows each token's name, its first characters, owner, scopes, expiry and when it was last used (time and IP).
Tokens issued by [the OAuth server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth) carry an `oauth: <client id>` label. Click **Revoke** and
confirm to delete one; anything using it stops working at once.

App users who aren't superusers manage their own tokens through the [REST API](#rest-api).

### From the command line

The `token` command works on the local data dir, like `superuser`, so you can set up tokens before the first serve:

```bash
pocketone token create --superuser admin@example.com --name ci --scope deploy --ttl 720h   # prints the secret
pocketone token create --collection users --record user@example.com --name script
pocketone token list                                    # every token, or one owner's with an owner flag
pocketone token revoke <id> [<id>...]
pocketone token revoke --all --superuser admin@example.com
pocketone token scopes
```

Pick the owner with `--superuser <email>`, or `--collection <name> --record <id or email>`. `--scope` can be repeated;
without `--ttl` the token never expires.

### Using a token

```bash
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer pbt_…" https://myapp.example.com/api/collections/notes/records
```

- An invalid, revoked or expired token leaves the request signed out, like an invalid PocketBase token.
- A scoped token used outside its scopes gets `403` ("This API token's scopes (…) don't allow this request.").
- A token can't be exchanged for a PocketBase auth token (`auth-refresh` and `impersonate` refuse it), so revoking a
  token really ends its access.
- Expired tokens are deleted once a day. Deleting an account deletes its tokens.

### In the logs

- A rejected token is logged at debug level: `tokens: rejected API token`.
- The daily cleanup logs `tokens: deleted expired tokens` with a count when it deletes any, and
  `tokens: delete expired` as a warning if it fails.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [OAuth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth) (in Tokens) | Its access tokens are API tokens, issued with the client's id, the granted scopes and, when asked for, an audience. They show up under Settings → API tokens and can be revoked there. The OAuth server needs Tokens on the app. |
| [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) | An agent's OAuth sign-in to `/mcp` is an API token bound to `/mcp` that never expires; revoke it to disconnect the agent. Tool calls run as the token's owner. A full-access token's calls hold every registered scope; a token limited to scopes on the consent page has its calls checked like requests with those scopes (`WithScopes`). |
| [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | Registers `deploy` and `deploy:read`; a `deploy` token is what CI uses. |
| [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes) | `pocketone login` takes a pasted API token when the remote has no OAuth server. In CI, put a token in `P1_TOKEN` (or `P1_TOKEN_<REMOTE>`). remote/v1's whoami (`/api/_c/remote/v1`) reports a token's id and scopes, whatever its scopes. |
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | Add `tokens.New(tokens.Config{})` to the host's extensions and every instance gets its own tokens, routes and screen. Per instance, `extensions: {tokens: {enabled: false}}` turns it off and `collections: [...]` picks who may own tokens. The stock `pocketone` binary doesn't add it to pocker instances. |

### Building on Tokens

**Register a scope from Go.** Extensions register their scopes on the app, usually on bootstrap, and guard their routes:

```go
tk := tokens.For(app)
tk.MustRegisterScope(tokens.Scope{
    Name:        "notes:write",
    Description: "Change notes",
    Paths:       []string{"/api/collections/notes/records"},
    Methods:     []string{"POST", "PATCH", "DELETE"}, // optional
    Collections: []string{"users"},                   // optional: who may hold it
})
se.Router.POST("/api/notes/archive", h).Bind(apis.RequireAuth(), tokens.RequireScope("notes:write"))
```

- **Guards.** A Go scope can add `Match func(*core.RequestEvent) bool`: a token with the scope also works on any
  request it returns true for. It runs before the owner is loaded, so it may look only at the request.
- **Shared scopes.** Registering a name again merges its paths, methods, guards and collections, so several extensions
  can share one scope.
- **Read the token on a request.** `tokens.FromRequest(e)` returns the token a request used (nil for a PocketBase
  auth token), with its `Owner`, `Scopes` and `Audience`. `tokens.HasScope(e, "x")` is true for PocketBase auth
  tokens and unscoped API tokens.
- **Without importing this package.** Other extensions use the [tokens/v1](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/tokens/v1/tokens.go)
  contract instead: `tokensv1.Contract.Of(app)` registers scopes (`RegisterScope`), lists them and checks `Reaches`;
  `tokensv1.FromRequest(e)` is the request's token (its `Grant`: owner, scopes, audience, client id);
  `tokensv1.WithScopes` limits in-process requests. Deploy and MCP work this way. The `X-Token-Scope-*` headers work
  for rules and JS.
- **Audience.** A token created with `CreateOptions.Audience` (the OAuth server sets it from the RFC 8707 `resource`
  parameter) only works under that URL's path, plus remote/v1's whoami (`/api/_c/remote/v1`); elsewhere it gets `403`. When the audience has
  a path (like `https://host/mcp`), the token works there whatever its scopes: the scopes limit what that endpoint
  does on the token's behalf (MCP passes them on with `WithScopes`), not the endpoint itself.
- **Limit in-process requests.** `tokens.WithScopes(ctx, scopes)` returns a context whose requests are checked like a
  token limited to `scopes`, whatever credential they carry: `403` where the scopes don't reach, and only those
  scopes in the `X-Token-Scope-*` headers and `HasScope`. Requests made inside them with the same context inherit
  the limit, and a nested `WithScopes` only narrows it. No client value can set it. `tokens.ScopesFromContext(ctx)`
  reads it. `Reaches(scopes, method, pattern)` says whether scopes could cover a route pattern (`{name}` segments
  match anything), and `Scope.Infrastructure()` whether a scope only reaches contract APIs (`/api/_c/`).

**Go API.** `tokens.For(app)` returns the service: `Create(owner, CreateOptions{Name, Scopes, Expires, ClientId,
Audience})` returns the secret and record; also `Verify(secret)`, `List(owner)`, `Get(id)`, `Revoke(id)`,
`RevokeAll(owner)`, `DeleteExpired()`, `RegisterScope`, `MustRegisterScope`, `Scopes()`, `Collections()` and
`AllowedCollection(c)`. `tokens.BindJS(vm, app)` adds `$tokens`; the extkit extension (`tokens.New`) also binds it.

**JS.** `$tokens.registerScope({name, description, paths, methods, collections})`, `$tokens.requireScope(name)`,
`$tokens.hasScope(e, name)`, `$tokens.ruleField(name)` and `$tokens.scopes()`.

### REST API (tokens/v1)

The [tokens/v1](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/tokens/v1/tokens.go) contract, at `/api/_c/tokens/v1`. Any signed-in account; superusers
see and manage everyone's.

| Route | What |
|---|---|
| `GET /api/_c/tokens/v1` | Your tokens. Superusers see all, or one owner's with `?ownerCollection=&owner=`. |
| `POST /api/_c/tokens/v1` | `{name, scopes, ttl \| expires}` (`ttl` in seconds, `expires` RFC 3339); superusers may add `ownerCollection` and `owner`. Returns the secret once. A scoped token can only create tokens within its own scopes. |
| `DELETE /api/_c/tokens/v1/{id}` | Revoke one. |
| `POST /api/_c/tokens/v1/revoke-all` | Revoke all of yours (superusers: `{ownerCollection, owner}`). |
| `GET /api/_c/tokens/v1/scopes` | The registered scopes, who may own tokens, and whether you can. |

Owners can also list, view and delete their own tokens through the records API of `_tokens`.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](example/main.go) runs one app with API tokens: Settings → API tokens, the token API (`/api/_c/tokens/v1`) and the `token` command.

```go
// Command example runs one PocketOne app with API tokens: Settings → API tokens in the dashboard, the token API (/api/_c/tokens/v1)
// and the `token` command.
//
//	go run ./example serve
//	go run ./example token create --superuser admin@example.com --name ci
//	curl -H "Authorization: Bearer pbt_..." http://127.0.0.1:8090/api/collections
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"log"
	"net/http"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/apis"
	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/tokens"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"

	tk := tokens.MustRegister(app, tokens.Config{
		Collections: []string{"_superusers", "users"}, // who may own tokens
	})
	// an extension's scope: a token limited to "hello" only authenticates under /api/hello; a JWT or unscoped token
	// holds it too, and every request that holds it carries X-Token-Scope-Hello: 1 for rules and hooks
	tk.MustRegisterScope(tokens.Scope{Name: "hello", Description: "Say hello", Paths: []string{"/api/hello"}, Methods: []string{"GET"}})

	app.OnServe().BindFunc(func(se *core.ServeEvent) error {
		se.Router.GET("/api/hello", func(e *core.RequestEvent) error {
			return e.JSON(http.StatusOK, map[string]any{"hello": e.Auth.Email()})
		}).Bind(apis.RequireAuth(), tokens.RequireScope("hello"))
		return se.Next()
	})

	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## Go config

```go
tokens.MustRegister(app, tokens.Config{
    Collections: []string{"_superusers", "users"}, // who may own tokens (default: every auth collection)
    MaxTTL:      0,                                // cap on a token's lifetime (0: none)
})
```

With `MaxTTL` set, a token asked for with no expiry or a later one gets the cap instead. If you narrow `Collections`,
The OAuth server can only sign in accounts of those collections.

## How it works

- Tokens live in the `_tokens` collection: owner (collection id and record id), name, `hash` (SHA-256 of the secret;
  the secret itself is never stored), display prefix, scopes, expiry, last use (time and IP), OAuth client id and
  audience.
- The bearer check is a middleware that runs just before PocketBase's own auth middleware; a second one, right after
  it, sets the scope headers. Last use is written at most once a minute per token.
- [`example/main.go`](example/main.go) runs one app where superusers and users may own tokens, with a `hello` scope
  for `GET /api/hello`. Try it with `go run ./example serve` and
  `go run ./example token create --superuser admin@example.com --name ci` (logins from
  [devusers](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/devusers/devusers.go): admin@example.com / password, user@example.com / password).

---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth

# OAuth

[Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) includes an OAuth 2.1 authorization server whose access tokens are API tokens: the
[oauth/v1](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/oauth/v1/oauth.go) contract. `pocketone login` signs in to it in the browser (or with a code on
another device), and MCP clients such as Claude or ChatGPT connectors register themselves and connect. Superusers and
app users sign in on your app's own pages, through PocketBase's own auth endpoints.

## Install

It comes with Tokens, which is in every app's [standard set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard). There's nothing to install or turn
on. Its endpoints are under `/api/_c/oauth/v1/` (see [Endpoints](#endpoints)); its metadata is at
`/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`.

In your own Go build, configure it through Tokens:

```go
set := standard.New()
set.Tokens = tokens.New(tokens.Config{OAuth: tokens.OAuthConfig{
	Branding: tokens.Branding{Accent: "#4f46e5"},
}})
```

`tokens.Config{OAuth: tokens.OAuthConfig{Disabled: true}}` leaves it out.

## Configure

There is no `pocketone.yaml` section, flag or environment variable for OAuth Server. In `pocketone`:
- superusers and every auth collection may sign in;
- access tokens last 30 days, refresh tokens 180 days (renewed on each refresh);
- tokens for [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) never expire, since MCP turns that on for `/mcp`;
- client self-registration (`POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/register`) is on, since MCP turns it on;
- Claude and Claude Code connect without registering (their client metadata documents from `claude.ai` and
  `claude.com` are trusted).

A Go build can change these (see [Go config](#go-config)).

### Sign-in methods

The pages offer exactly the methods each auth collection has on, so you set them where you always do: the
collection's options in the dashboard (**Collections →** the collection **→ Options**).
- **Password**, **One-time password** (an emailed code) and **OAuth2** providers each get their own form or button.
- **Multi-factor authentication** adds a second step.
- The collection's auth rule (for example `verified = true`) applies.

OAuth2 providers (Google, GitHub, …) are offered to app users only; PocketBase doesn't allow them for superusers.
**Register `<your app's URL>/api/_c/oauth/v1/provider/callback` as a redirect URI with each provider.**

The pages show **Settings → Application → Application name**.

### Behind a proxy

The server names itself (the issuer) after the scheme and host the browser used, with `https` when the request is TLS
or `X-Forwarded-Proto` says so. If a proxy rewrites the host, set `Config.Issuer` in a Go build so the issuer and the
provider callback URL stay stable.

### Scopes

A client may ask for any scope registered with [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens#scopes), including your own from
`$tokens.registerScope`. `offline_access` is accepted (refresh tokens are always issued).

The consent page lets the user decide: **Full access** (no scopes: the account's full rights) or **Only these**, with a
box for each scope. The scopes the client asked for start ticked; the others the account may hold are there to tick,
except ones that only reach contract APIs under `/api/_c/` (like `deploy`), which appear only when asked for. With no scopes
asked, **Full access** starts selected. The token gets exactly what was ticked, and the token response's `scope` says
which.

### Your own sign-in pages

The built-in pages (sign-in, second step, one-time code, consent, device code, done, error) follow the system's light
or dark mode and work on phones. To change them, eject them as [PocketPages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages) templates:

```bash
pocketone oauth eject           # --force overwrites files you already have
```

It writes `signin.ejs`, `mfa.ejs`, `otp.ejs`, `consent.ejs`, `device.ejs`, `done.ejs`, `error.ejs` and the shared
`head.ejs`, `foot.ejs` and `hidden.ejs` (with the CSS) to `pb_pages/_private/oauth/`, and prints each file. From then
on the server renders your templates; a missing one falls back to the built-in page, so delete them to go back.
`_private` keeps them from being served as routes. See [Custom page templates](#custom-page-templates) for the data
they get.

## Use

### Signing in

Whenever a client sends someone to your app (`pocketone login`, Claude, an app of yours), they see:

1. **Sign in to <app name>**: the form for app users (`users` first; with several user collections, a tab for
   each). At the bottom, **Sign in as a superuser** switches to the superuser form, which looks clearly different:
   a **Superuser** badge, **Superuser sign-in**, its own colors and a warning. **Sign in as a user instead** goes back.
2. **One more step** when the account has MFA, offering its other methods. After a password, when an emailed code is
   the only method left, it's sent right away.
3. **Check your email** for an emailed code.
4. The consent page: the client's name, the account, whether the client will act as a user (and which collection) or
   as a superuser, and the access: **Full access** or **Only these** scopes (see [Scopes](#scopes)). Click **Allow** or
   **Deny**, or **Not <email>? Use another account**.

With no user collection allowed, the superuser form is the only one. A browser stays signed in to these pages for 15
minutes. Failed attempts are limited to 10 per IP in 5 minutes.

On another device (over SSH, say), the client shows a code like `WDJB-MJHT`. Open
`https://<your app>/api/_c/oauth/v1/device/verify`, enter it under **Connect a device**, sign in and allow. Codes last 10 minutes.

### Log in from the command line

```bash
pocketone login prod
```

With OAuth Server on the remote, [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes) opens your browser on the pages above, or shows a
device code when there's no browser (`--device` asks for one). The client is the built-in `pocketone-cli`, named
**pocketone CLI** on the consent page (the name follows the command, so another build shows its own).

### See and revoke what's connected

Every sign-in creates an API token named "<client> (OAuth)". They're listed under **Settings → API tokens** with an
`oauth: <client id>` label; click **Revoke** to disconnect a client. Revoking the access token also ends its refresh
token. A client can revoke its own tokens at `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/revoke`, which `pocketone logout` does.

### Register clients

Claude and the CLI need no registration, and MCP clients register themselves. For your own app:

```bash
pocketone oauth clients add --name "My app" --redirect https://myapp.example.com/callback
pocketone oauth clients add --name "Desktop" --redirect http://127.0.0.1/callback --public
pocketone oauth clients list
pocketone oauth clients rm <client_id>
```

`add` prints the client id, and the secret once for a confidential client. `--public` makes a client with no secret
(PKCE only), for desktop and mobile apps. `--redirect` can be repeated.

Redirect URIs must be `https`, `http` on a loopback address, or an app's custom scheme. Loopback URIs match any port
(RFC 8252); others must match exactly.

### In the logs

- `tokens: oauth: this collection may sign in but can't own API tokens; add it to tokens.Config.Collections`, once per
  collection, when Tokens is narrowed in a Go build. The page then says signing in with that account type "isn't set
  up on this server yet".
- `tokens: oauth: auth methods` (error) when a collection's sign-in methods can't be read.
- `tokens: oauth: cleanup` (warning) when the half-hourly removal of expired codes fails.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) | It's part of Tokens. Access tokens are API tokens owned by whoever signed in, with the client's id, the granted scopes and the audience. Every registered scope can be requested. |
| [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes) | remote/v1's whoami lists `oauth/v1` (and the `oauth` feature, its metadata); `pocketone login` then signs in in the browser (loopback redirect with PKCE) or with a device code, and renews through the refresh token. |
| [MCP](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mcp) | MCP points clients here from its protected resource metadata, turns on self-registration, and makes tokens bound to `/mcp` never expire. Tool calls run as whoever signed in. |
| [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | `pocketone login` gives the deploy commands a token for the account that signed in. |
| [Pages](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pages) | `pocketone oauth eject` writes the pages as PocketPages templates, rendered from then on. |

Under [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) every instance has it, through the standard set.

### Audience (RFC 8707)

A `resource` parameter on `/api/_c/oauth/v1/authorize`, `/api/_c/oauth/v1/device` or `/api/_c/oauth/v1/token` (a URL on this server) binds the
access token to it: the token then only works under that URL's path. So a token issued for `/mcp` can't deploy, and a
deploy token can't drive MCP. Refreshed tokens keep it.

### Building on the OAuth server

- **Go API.** `tokens.OAuth(app)` returns the server. `Issuer(e)` is its public base URL;
  `EnableDynamicRegistration()` turns on `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/register`; `SetAccessTTL("/mcp", 0)` sets the lifetime of
  tokens bound to a resource (0: never expire). `FindClient`, `ListClients`, `AddClient` and `RemoveClient` manage
  clients.
- **Scopes.** Register a scope with Tokens (Go or `$tokens.registerScope`) and clients can ask for it; nothing else
  is needed.
- **Render the pages yourself.** `Config.Render(e, page, data)` renders any page (return `handled=false` to fall
  back), with `PageData`. It wins over ejected templates.

## Example

The OAuth server is on wherever Tokens is (its [example](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/tokens/example/main.go) runs it). To brand it and let MCP connectors
register themselves:

```go
set := standard.New()
set.Tokens = tokens.New(tokens.Config{OAuth: tokens.OAuthConfig{
	DynamicRegistration: true, // MCP connectors register themselves (ext/mcp turns this on anyway)
	Branding:            tokens.Branding{Accent: "#4f46e5", Footer: "Example OAuth server"},
}})
app := set.NewApp(pocketbase.Config{}, jsvm.Config{})
```

## Endpoints

| Path | What |
|---|---|
| `GET /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` | Metadata (RFC 8414). The issuer is `Config.Issuer`, else the request's own scheme and host. |
| `GET/POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/authorize` | Sign-in and consent pages. Authorization code with PKCE (S256 only; required). |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/token` | `authorization_code`, `refresh_token` and `urn:ietf:params:oauth:grant-type:device_code`. Refresh rotates without logouts: the old access token lives out its time, and the old refresh token works again for 2 minutes, so two processes refreshing at once both succeed. |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/device`, `GET/POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/device/verify` | Device flow (RFC 8628): codes like `WDJB-MJHT`, valid 10 minutes. |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/revoke` | Revocation (RFC 7009): an access token or a refresh token (revokes both). |
| `GET/POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/provider/callback` | Where OAuth2 providers send the browser back after sign-in. |
| `POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/register` | Dynamic client registration (RFC 7591), when `DynamicRegistration` is on or an extension called `EnableDynamicRegistration()` (MCP does). Public clients by default. |

Protected resource metadata (RFC 9728) belongs to the resource: MCP serves `/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource`.

## Clients

- **`pocketone-cli`** is built in: public, any `http://127.0.0.1:<port>/…` or `[::1]` redirect, device codes. It's
  what `pocketone login` uses.
- **Client ID metadata documents (CIMD):** an `https://` client id is fetched as a JSON document (`client_id` must
  equal the URL; its `client_name` and `redirect_uris` are used; public clients only; cached 10 minutes). Only
  `Config.CIMDHosts` are trusted (default `claude.ai`, `claude.com`); the metadata says
  `client_id_metadata_document_supported`.
- Registered clients live in `_tokens_oauth_clients`; codes, device codes and refresh tokens in `_tokens_oauth_codes`.

## How sign-in works

The pages never check passwords or codes themselves. Each step calls PocketBase's own auth endpoint in-process,
through the app's router, so the collection's auth rule, MFA, rate limits, superuser IP limits and every
`onRecordAuth*Request` hook apply as for the REST API, and the record the endpoint returns is the one signed in:

- password: `POST /api/collections/{c}/auth-with-password`;
- emailed code: `POST …/request-otp`, then `POST …/auth-with-otp`;
- OAuth2: the browser goes to the provider with the state and PKCE from `GET …/auth-methods`, comes back to
  `/api/_c/oauth/v1/provider/callback`, and `POST …/auth-with-oauth2` completes it (account linking and sign-up are
  PocketBase's);
- MFA: when an auth call answers 401 with an `mfaId`, the second page passes it along.

Only collections with a sign-in method on are offered. Access tokens are owned by the signed-in record, so every
collection that may sign in must also be allowed by Tokens (its default is every auth collection). The session is a
15-minute HttpOnly cookie on `/api/_c/oauth/v1`; forms carry a CSRF token; a provider round trip keeps its state in a signed
10-minute cookie.

## Go config

```go
tokens.New(tokens.Config{OAuth: tokens.OAuthConfig{
    Collections:         nil,                  // who may sign in; default: _superusers + every auth collection
    AccessTTL:           30 * 24 * time.Hour,  // default; per resource with srv.SetAccessTTL("/mcp", 0)
    RefreshTTL:          180 * 24 * time.Hour, // default, renewed on each refresh
    DynamicRegistration: false,                // POST /api/_c/oauth/v1/register (MCP turns it on)
    CIMDHosts:           nil,                  // default claude.ai, claude.com; an empty non-nil slice turns CIMD off
    Issuer:              "",                   // public base URL; default: the request's scheme and host
    Branding:            tokens.Branding{LogoURL: "/logo.svg", Accent: "#4f46e5", Footer: "Acme Inc."},
}})
```

`Branding` also takes a `Name` (default: Settings → Application name). `Accent` is the button color (default
`#16161a`).

## Custom page templates

Ejected templates get `ctx.data`: `PageData` in camelCase (`data.appName`, `data.action`, `data.hidden`,
`data.csrf`, `data.clientName`, `data.scopes`, `data.scopeChoices`, `data.superuser`, `data.providers`, `data.error`, …).
- Every POST form must include `include('/oauth/hidden')` and a `step` button.
- Steps: `password`, `request_otp`, `otp`, `oauth2:<provider>`, `use:<collection>` (switch forms; `use:` is the
  default user form), `allow`, `deny`, `switch`.
- Sign-in forms post `collection`; the MFA and code pages also post `mfa_id` / `otp_id`.
- Consent posts `access` = `full`, or `limited` with a `grant` field per ticked scope (from `data.scopeChoices`:
  `name`, `description`, `checked`). A consent form without `access` grants what the client asked for.

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy

# Deploy

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Send your project's code to a running app from your own machine: `pb_hooks`, `pb_migrations`, `pb_pages`,
`pb_public`, packages and the production `node_modules` tree. Only changed files are uploaded and the app swaps them
in; `restart` applies new migrations and packages. `pocketone dev` keeps your folder and the app in step both ways and
streams the app's logs; `pull` and `logs` work the other way.

```bash
pocketone link https://myapp.example.com   # add the remote and sign in (Remotes)
pocketone deploy                           # upload what changed
pocketone logs
```

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Deploy is built into `pocketone` and **on** in both directions: every app it serves accepts deploys from its
superusers, and the `deploy`, `dev`, `pull`, `logs` and `restart` commands are there to deploy to other apps. There's
nothing to install.

In your own Go build, register it before the app starts. [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes) gives the commands their
remotes and logins, and [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) lets you deploy with API tokens:

```go
app := pocketbase.New()
extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{
	tokens.New(tokens.Config{}),   // optional: API tokens with the deploy scope
	remotes.New(remotes.Config{}), // remote/v1 (whoami, restart, logs), login
	deploy.NewExtension(deploy.Config{}), // deploy/v1 + deploy/dev/pull/logs/restart commands
}, nil, nil)
app.Start()
```

The [standard set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard) does this for you.

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/deploy`. `deploy.Config{DisableServer: true}` keeps only the
commands, for a binary that deploys elsewhere but must not accept deploys.

## Configure

There is no `pocketone.yaml` section, flag or settings screen. Defaults on the receiving app:

- **Who may deploy:** superusers. You sign in with `pocketone login` (see [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes)) or use an
  API token. A token needs the `deploy` scope (or no scopes); `deploy:read` allows reading files and logs only.
- **Where files land:** next to `pb_data`, PocketBase's usual layout (`pb_hooks/`, `pb_migrations/`,
  `pb_public/`, `node_modules/` beside it).
- **Upload store:** uploaded files and past deploys are kept in `.pb_deploy/` next to `pb_data`. It's outside
  `pb_data`, so backups skip it, and it's never deployed.

On your machine, the commands use the project's remotes and saved logins from [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes). In CI,
set `P1_TOKEN` (or `P1_TOKEN_<REMOTE>`) instead of signing in.

## Use

All commands take an optional remote name or URL; without one they use the project's default remote. Run them from
your project folder (or any folder below it).

### `deploy`

```bash
pocketone deploy                      # to the default remote
pocketone deploy prod -m "fix signup" # to the remote "prod", with a note
pocketone deploy --restart            # and restart if migrations or packages changed (CI)
pocketone deploy --dry-run            # list what would be sent, send nothing
pocketone deploy --out /tmp/set       # write the files to a folder instead
```

You'll see how many files are deployed and how many are uploaded, then a line like
`Deployed <id>: 3 changed, 0 deleted, 41 unchanged.` With nothing changed it says `Up to date: no changes.`

| Flag | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--restart` | Restart the app after the files are in, when migrations or packages changed. |
| `--dry-run` | List what would be deployed; deploy nothing. |
| `--out <dir>` | Write the deploy set to a local folder instead of deploying. |
| `-i`, `--include` | Add include patterns to the default set. |
| `-e`, `--exclude` | Exclude patterns (`pb_data` is always excluded). |
| `--node-modules` | Ship the production `node_modules` tree (the default when there's a `package.json`). |
| `--no-node-modules` | Don't ship `node_modules`; leave the remote's alone. |
| `--commit <sha>` | Commit to record. Default: `$GITHUB_SHA`, `$CI_COMMIT_SHA`, or git `HEAD`. |
| `-m`, `--message` | A note to record with the deploy. |
| `-v`, `--verbose` | List every file. |

**What's sent:** files matching `pb_*` and `pb_*/**/*` except `pb_data`, plus `package.json`, `bun.lock(b)` and
`patches/**`. Dotfiles are included (`pb_public/.well-known`); `.git*` files and symlinks are skipped.

**Packages:** with a `package.json`, the production `node_modules` tree is collected the way Node resolves it (hoisted
npm and bun, pnpm's store, workspace links; never devDependencies) and shipped as plain files, so plain JS hooks can
`require` npm packages. The remote then owns its root `node_modules`: packages you no longer ship are removed there.

**Restarts:** files are swapped in while the app runs, each rename atomic, and deploy never restarts the app on its
own. `pb_pages` and `pb_public` are read from disk on each request, and hooks reload by themselves (PocketBase's
`--hooksWatch`, Pocker's watcher). Migrations and packages apply only when the app starts, so a deploy that changes
them says `Migrations or packages changed` and leaves the restart to you: pass `--restart` (the app restarts once,
after the whole batch is in, and you hear if it fails to start), run `pocketone restart`, or type `r` in `dev`. So
does the first deploy that creates `pb_hooks`, since a watcher only sees folders that existed when the app started.

### `restart`

```bash
pocketone restart prod
```

Restarts the app so it applies new migrations and packages, and tells you if it fails to start. An app that isn't
running (a sleeping Pocker instance) is left alone; it applies them when it starts.

### `dev`

```bash
pocketone dev
pocketone dev prod --prefer local   # first sync: upload yours where both sides differ
```

Keeps the project folder and the remote in step, both ways, and streams the remote's logs. Stop it with Ctrl+C.

| What | Direction |
|---|---|
| `pb_hooks`, `pb_migrations`, `pb_pages`, `pb_public` and other `pb_*` folders | both ways |
| `package.json`, `bun.lock(b)`, `patches/` | both ways |
| `node_modules` | uploaded only, when `package.json` or the lockfile changes |
| `pb_data` | never (it's the app's live data) |

- **Your edits** go up half a second after you save.
- **Changes on the remote**, such as the migrations the dashboard writes when you edit a collection, come down within
  a few seconds (`--poll`, default 5s). `dev` asks the remote for one hash and only looks further when it changed, so
  a large `pb_public` costs nothing while it's quiet.
- **Restarts:** `dev` never restarts the app by itself. Hooks reload by themselves, pages and public files are live on
  the next request. After you upload a migration or new packages, `dev` says so: type `r` and Enter to restart the app
  and apply them. Migrations that come down are already applied on the remote.
- **Deletes** go both ways too.
- **Changed on both sides:** your copy wins and is uploaded; the remote's is saved in `.pocketone/conflicts/` and
  `dev` says so.
- **First run:** files that exist on only one side are copied to the other. If a file differs on both sides, `dev`
  lists them and asks whether to keep yours or take the remote's; `--prefer local|remote` answers in advance.

`dev` keeps what it last synced in `.pocketone/sync.json` (add `.pocketone/` to `.gitignore`). List files to leave
out, such as ones your hooks generate, in `.pocketoneignore`, one gitignore-style pattern per line.

| Flag | What it does |
|---|---|
| `--prefer local\|remote` | First sync: who wins where both sides differ (default: ask). |
| `--poll <duration>` | How often to check the remote (default 5s). |
| `--push-only` | Only upload, the way `dev` used to work. Also used by itself for remotes without two-way sync. |
| `--no-logs` | Don't stream the remote's logs. |

It takes the same file flags as `deploy`.

### `pull`

```bash
pocketone pull prod                              # pb_hooks, pb_migrations, pb_pages, pb_public, package.json
pocketone pull prod pb_hooks pb_public/index.html
pocketone pull prod --dry-run
```

Downloads files from a remote into the project. `pb_data` is only reachable on an instance that's powered off, so a
single app (always running while it answers) refuses it.

### `logs`

```bash
pocketone logs prod
pocketone logs prod -n 20
```

Replays the last 100 lines (`-n`, `--lines`, 0 to 1000), then follows. Requests show as `GET /url → 200 (1.2 ms)` and
errors are marked `ERR`. PocketBase writes its logs in batches, so lines show up a few seconds late. The stream
reconnects by itself if it drops.

### Deploy history

Every deploy is recorded in the `_deploys` collection of the receiving app: status, file counts, bytes, commit,
message, source, token name, superuser and any error. Superusers can browse it in the dashboard.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes) | Gives the commands their remotes, saved logins and CI tokens. The commands find deploy/v1 in the remote's whoami, and `restart` and `logs` use its remote/v1 (deploy requires it). |
| [OAuth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth) (in Tokens) | `pocketone login` signs in through the browser when the remote runs it. |
| [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) | Deploy registers the `deploy` and `deploy:read` scopes, so you can make API tokens for CI that can only deploy or only read. Add `remote` for `--restart` and `remote:read` for `dev`'s logs. |
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | The same API runs for many instances with your own backend: build it with `deploy.New` (below). PocketHost does this. |

### Building on Deploy

- **Go client.** `deploy.NewClient(ctx, rc)` takes a remote/v1 client (`remoteclient.Open`, from
  [ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient)) and finds its deploy API.
  `Deploy`, `Pull`, `Collect`, `Watch` and `NewSyncer` (two-way sync: `Sync`, `RemoteChanged`) are the commands'
  building blocks.
- **Your own host.** `deploy.New(deploy.Options{Prefix, Backend, Instances, PBRoot, DataRoot, PlatformPaths})`
  builds the API; mount `api.Wrap(next)`. `Backend` decides which instance a request is for (`Lookup(r)`), who it
  acts as (`Authenticate(r, inst)` → `Auth{UserID, Scopes, Via, TokenLabel}`, an `*AuthError`, or `ErrNoAccess` for a
  404) and records history. `Instances` is pocker's Manager (stop, swap, start). Serve it as deploy/v1 for the host's
  instances (`deployv1.Contract.ProvideForInstances`, `extkit.HostRoutes` in `multisite.Host.InstanceRoutes`); restart and logs are the host's remote/v1.
- **Restarts.** Your `Instances` should reload an instance by itself when its `pb_hooks` change (pocker's Manager
  does); deploy only restarts through it when a client asks (`Client.Restart`, or `DeployOptions.Restart`).
- **Discovery.** Deploy provides the [deploy/v1](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/deploy/v1/deploy.go) contract, which whoami lists, so
  clients find it at `/api/_c/deploy/v1`. A multisite host can provide it for its instances instead.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](example/main.go) is an app that both accepts deploys and makes them: the deploy API, API tokens, remotes and the deploy commands. Its comment walks through a first deploy against itself.

```go
// Command example is a PocketOne app that accepts deploys and can deploy: deploy/v1 (/api/_c/deploy/v1), remote/v1
// (restart, logs), API tokens, and the deploy/dev/pull/logs/restart commands.
//
//	go run ./example serve --http=127.0.0.1:8090                  # the remote
//	cd myproject && mkdir pb_hooks && echo 'routerAdd("GET", "/hi", (e) => e.string(200, "hi"))' > pb_hooks/main.pb.js
//	go run ./example link http://127.0.0.1:8090 --email admin@example.com   # password: password
//	go run ./example deploy
//	curl http://127.0.0.1:8090/hi
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/deploy"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/jsvm"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/remotes"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/tokens"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"

	// registered through their contracts (the standard set does this for you); deploys land next to pb_data
	exts := []extkit.Extension{tokens.New(tokens.Config{}), remotes.New(remotes.Config{}), deploy.NewExtension(deploy.Config{})}
	if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, exts, nil, nil); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{}) // deployed pb_hooks and pb_migrations

	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## Deploy API

deploy/v1, at `/api/_c/deploy/v1` (superusers, see Configure): the files only, on an app or a host. Whoami, restart
and logs are remote/v1's (`/api/_c/remote/v1`), which deploy requires.

| Route | What it does |
|---|---|
| `POST /check` | Takes a manifest, returns the hashes the server is missing. |
| `POST /blobs` | Gzipped `PHB1` bundles: `[sha256][uint32 length][bytes]`…, every hash verified, 64 MB per request. |
| `POST /commit` | Stage, swap in, record. `"restartNeeded": true` in the answer when migrations or packages wait for a restart; `"restart": true` in the request restarts after the swap. With `"partial": true` only the listed files (and `"delete"`) change. |
| `GET`/`DELETE /files` | List or delete files. |
| `GET`/`PUT /files/raw` | Download or upload one file. |
| `GET /tree` | One folder of the code set (`?path=`, default the root) with a hash over everything below it; `hashOnly=1` for just the hash. |

The protocol is the pockethost npm CLI's, so the same client deploys to PocketOne apps and PocketHost.

## How it works

- Go module `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/deploy`. [`example/main.go`](example/main.go) is an app that accepts
  deploys and can deploy (logins from [devusers](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/devusers/devusers.go): admin@example.com / password).
- A deploy is a hash diff: the client sends a manifest, uploads only the missing files in bundles, then commits.
- On a single app the files are swapped in while it runs; a restart (when a client asks) is `app.Restart()`, which
  re-executes the process (`Config.Restart` overrides it; not on Windows).
- `Config.Dir` and `Config.StoreDir` move the deploy folder and the upload store; `Config.Prefix` moves the API.
- Logs on a single app come from its own `_logs` table; entries at error level and above are marked as stderr.
- The `node_modules` collector is [`nodemodules`](nodemodules/nodemodules.go), a port of the npm CLI's.

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes

# Remotes

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Named remotes for the `pocketone` command: the apps a project deploys to, each signed in to once. Give an app a name
like `prod`, log in, and commands such as `pocketone deploy prod` know where to go and who you are.

```bash
pocketone remote add prod https://myapp.example.com
pocketone login prod
pocketone deploy prod          # Deploy
```

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Remotes is built into `pocketone` and **on**: the `remote`, `login`, `logout` and `link` commands are always there, and
every app provides [remote/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/all): whoami at `GET /api/_c/remote/v1` (so other machines can sign
in to it), status, restart and logs. There's nothing to install: it's in the [standard set](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/standard).

In your own Go build, use the standard set, or register it through its contracts yourself:

```go
app := pocketbase.New()
extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{remotes.New(remotes.Config{})}, nil, nil) // remote/v1; on *pocketbase.PocketBase also the commands
app.Start()
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/remotes`. Add [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) for API tokens and
[the OAuth server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth) for browser login.

## Configure

There is no `pocketone.yaml` section, flag or settings screen. Remotes keeps two files and reads a few environment
variables.

### The project's remotes

`.pocketbase/remotes.json` in the project holds names and URLs only, so commit it:

```json
{"default": "prod", "remotes": {"prod": {"url": "https://myapp.example.com"}}}
```

Commands find it by walking up from the current folder. It isn't a `pb_*` name, since `pb_*` folders are deployed.

### Saved logins

Logins are saved per user, keyed by URL, in `~/.config/pocketone/credentials.json` (mode 0600). Set
`P1_CONFIG_DIR` to use another folder; with `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` set, it's `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/pocketone/`.

### Environment variables

| Variable | What it does |
|---|---|
| `P1_TOKEN_<REMOTE>` | A token for one remote, for CI. The name is upper case, other characters as `_` (`P1_TOKEN_PROD`). |
| `P1_TOKEN` | A token for any remote. |
| `P1_CONFIG_DIR` | Where saved logins are kept. |

A token in the environment wins over a saved login. Every PocketOne variable starts with `P1_`, in every build (the
`pockethost` binary reads `P1_TOKEN` too). The `pocketone` folder comes from the command's name, so a build shipped
under another name keeps its logins apart (`~/.config/pockethost`).

## Use

### Manage remotes

```bash
pocketone remote add prod https://myapp.example.com --default
pocketone remote list            # names, URLs and who you're logged in as; * marks the default
pocketone remote default prod
pocketone remote rm staging      # the saved login stays; see logout
pocketone remote whoami prod     # who you are there, your token's scopes, and what the app offers
```

A URL without a scheme gets `https://`. The first remote you add becomes the default. A command that names no remote
uses the default, else the only remote, else the one called `default`. Any command also takes a URL in place of a
name: `pocketone deploy https://other.example.com`.

### Log in

```bash
pocketone login prod
```

`login` tries, in order (the command itself never asks for a password):

1. **The browser**, when the remote runs [the OAuth server](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth). Your browser opens, you sign in
   and approve, and the command finishes. Over SSH or without a display it shows a code to enter on another device
   instead; `--device` asks for that, and `--no-browser` prints the URL without opening it.
2. **A pasted token** (`pbt_...`, a PocketHost token, or a PocketBase auth token). At the prompt, paste it, or pass
   `--token <token>` or `--token-stdin`.

A browser login keeps a refresh token and renews itself when it's within a day of expiring.

You'll see `Logged in to https://myapp.example.com as admin@example.com (oauth).`

### Link in one step

```bash
pocketone link https://myapp.example.com
pocketone link https://myapp.pockethost.io ph_pat_...
```

`link` adds the remote (named `default`, or `--name`), makes it the default if there's none yet, and logs in. It takes
the same login flags.

### Log out

```bash
pocketone logout prod
```

Forgets the saved login. A browser login is also revoked on the remote (its refresh token); a pasted token stays
valid until you revoke it in the dashboard. If the remote can't be reached, it tells you to revoke it in the dashboard.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Deploy](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/deploy) | `deploy`, `dev` and `pull` resolve their remote and login through Remotes and find deploy/v1 in whoami's contracts; `restart` and `logs` use remote/v1. |
| [OAuth](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens/oauth) (in Tokens) | Provides oauth/v1, so whoami lists it; `login` then signs in through the browser (loopback redirect on 127.0.0.1 with PKCE) or a device code. |
| [Tokens](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tokens) | Provides the API tokens `login` takes when pasted. Whoami reports a token's id and scopes. |

### remote/v1

Remote control of an app, at `/api/_c/remote/v1`:

| Operation | Endpoint | Token scope |
|---|---|---|
| whoami | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1` | none needed (any token may ask who it is) |
| status | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/status` | `remote:read` |
| restart | `POST /api/_c/remote/v1/restart` | `remote` |
| logs | `GET /api/_c/remote/v1/logs?n=100` (server-sent events) | `remote:read` |

Whoami says who the request's credential is and what the app offers, so clients can discover it:

```json
{"auth": {"collection": "_superusers", "id": "…", "email": "admin@example.com"}, "via": "token",
 "tokenId": "…", "scopes": ["deploy", "remote"], "contracts": ["deploy/v1", "oauth/v1", "remote/v1", "tokens/v1"],
 "extensions": ["tokens", "remotes", "deploy"],
 "app": {"name": "Acme", "url": "https://myapp.example.com"}}
```

`via` is `token` for an API token, `jwt` for a PocketBase auth token, and empty with no credential (`auth` is then
`null`, and `extensions` is left out). `contracts` are the contract APIs the app offers, each at `/api/_c/<id>/`:
everything a client can use (oauth/v1's metadata is at `/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server`). Restart answers at once and restarts just after (under Pocker, only
that instance).

### Building on Remotes

- **remote/v1 client.** `remotev1.NewClient(url, token, httpClient)` (ext/contracts/remote/v1) calls whoami, status,
  restart and logs.
- **Go client.** The CLI client lives with the contract, in
  [`remoteclient`](../contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient) (ext/contracts/remote/v1/remoteclient), so other extensions'
  commands use it without importing this one. `remoteclient.Open(dir, name)` resolves a remote and its credential
  (environment first, then the saved login, renewing a browser login when due) and returns a `*remoteclient.Client`:
  base URL, bearer token, an HTTP client with short connect timeouts, and `JSON`, `NewRequest`, `Do` and `Whoami`.
  It also holds the linked project (`LoadProject`), saved logins (`LoadCredentials`) and the sign-ins
  (`LoginWithToken`, `OAuthLogin`). Deploy's commands build on it.
- **Commands.** `remotes.Commands()` returns the `remote`, `login`, `logout` and `link` commands, for a binary that
  isn't a `*pocketbase.PocketBase`. The rest of `remote` is generated: every operation of every contract the binary
  links is a `remote ...` command ([cli.commands/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/cli.commands/v1)), such as `remote status`,
  `remote restart`, `remote restore to --at -2h`.
- **Login.** `remotes.BrowserLogin` is the sign-in `login` tries first (`remoteclient.OAuthLogin`; tests replace it).

## Example

[`example/main.go`](example/main.go) is an app with remotes and API tokens. Run two copies and add one as a remote of the other; its comment has the commands.

```go
// Command example is a PocketOne app with remotes and API tokens: run two copies, add one as a remote of the other's
// project and sign in.
//
//	go run ./example serve --http=127.0.0.1:8090                # the "remote"
//	go run ./example remote add local http://127.0.0.1:8090    # in a project folder
//	go run ./example login local                               # browser sign-in: admin@example.com / password
//	go run ./example remote whoami
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"log"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/extkit"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/remotes"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/tokens"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"

	// registered through their contracts (the standard set does this for you): remotes provides remote/v1 (whoami at
	// /api/_c/remote/v1, status, restart, logs) and the remote/login/logout/link commands; tokens adds API tokens
	// and the OAuth server login signs in through
	if _, err := extkit.Setup(app, []extkit.Extension{tokens.New(tokens.Config{}), remotes.New(remotes.Config{})}, nil, nil); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```
