Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker

# Docker

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Run every instance on a host in its own container, with the official PocketBase or PocketOne binary of the version
the instance asks for. One host can serve PocketBase 0.23 and 0.36 and PocketOne side by side.

Docker is one of the two runtime providers of the multi-instance [multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite). The other is
[Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker), which runs every instance inside one process. A host runs exactly one of them.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Docker is built into `pocketone`. It needs a Docker daemon on the same machine; nothing else to install.

It's off until `pocketone.yaml` names it as the provider (below). Then `pocketone serve` runs the host instead of a
single app.

In your own Go build, add it to the host's extensions; it provides the [runtime/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/runtime/v1)
contract when `pocketone.yaml` has a `docker` section:

```go
h, err := multisite.FromConfig(multisite.Options{Resolve: cfg.ResolvePath,
	Extensions: []multisite.Extension{&docker.Provider{Resolve: cfg.ResolvePath}}})
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/docker`. Add `docker.NewCommand(...)` to your root command for the
`docker seed` and `docker update` commands.

## Configure

Add a `multisite` section (host mode) and a `docker` section to `pocketone.yaml`. Listeners (`server`), instances
(`instances`) and the firewall are the host's sections. With pocker linked too, both run: each instance on the one
its record names (`runtime: docker`), else the first that serves its version; `providers: { runtime/v1: [docker] }`
keeps docker alone.

```yaml
multisite: {}
docker:
  image: alpine:3.20                 # base image the binaries run in
  binaries: /var/lib/pocketbase      # release binary cache
  root: /var/lib/instances           # one folder per instance: <root>/<id>
  versions: ["pb:0.23", "pb:0.36", "p1:0.0"]
  default_version: "pb:0.36.*"
  idle_ttl: 10m
  max_concurrent_starts: 4
instances:
  file: ./instances.yaml
```

`image`, `binaries` and `root` are required.

**Versions.** An instance picks its binary with the prefix of its `version`: `pb:` is upstream PocketBase, `p1:` is
PocketOne, no prefix means `pb:`. `versions` lists the minors the host serves; the newest cached patch that matches
wins. A version that isn't listed gets a clear 503. Upstream PocketBase 0.22 and older are refused unless you lower
`min_upstream` and keep those releases in the cache yourself.

**Per instance** (`instances.yaml` or a mothership): `version`, `secrets` (passed as environment), `encryption_key`,
`dev`, and `dir` to put its folder somewhere other than `<root>/<id>`. An instance with `runtime` set to anything but
`docker` isn't served here.

**Limits and hardening** are optional: `nano_cpus`, `pids_limit`, `nofile`, `cap_drop` and `no_new_privileges`.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `docker:`

Runtime provider docker: each instance in its own container with the PocketBase (pb:) or PocketOne (p1:) binary of its version (image, binary cache and manifest, instance root, default version, idle stop, limits).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `socket` | string |  | The Docker socket. Default $DOCKER_HOST when it is unix://, else /var/run/docker.sock. |
| `image` | string |  | Base image the binaries run in, such as alpine:3.20. Required; pulled when missing. |
| `binaries` | string |  | Folder of the release binary cache and its releases.json. Required. |
| `versions` | list of string |  | The minors this host serves, such as pb:0.36 or p1:0.0 (latest patch of each, from docker update). |
| `root` | string |  | Folder with one folder per instance (<root>/<id>). Required. |
| `home` | string |  | The instance folder inside the container. Default /home/pockethost. |
| `default_version` | string |  | Version for instances that name none, such as p1:0.0.*. Empty: such instances fail. |
| `min_upstream` | string |  | Oldest upstream PocketBase release served. Default 0.23.0; lower it only for releases you cache yourself. |
| `idle_ttl` | duration |  | Stop a container after this long without requests. Default 10m. |
| `max_concurrent_starts` | int |  | Containers starting at once. Default 4. |
| `start_timeout` | duration |  | How long a container gets to answer its health check. Default 60s. |
| `nano_cpus` | int |  | CPU limit per container in billionths of a CPU (1000000000 = one CPU). 0: no limit. |
| `pids_limit` | int |  | Process limit per container. 0: Docker's default. |
| `nofile` | list of int |  | Open-file limit per container: [soft, hard]. Empty: Docker's default. |
| `cap_drop` | list of string |  | Linux capabilities to drop, such as [ALL]. |
| `no_new_privileges` | bool |  | Set no-new-privileges on every container. |
| `network` | string |  | Docker network for the containers. Default the bridge. |
| `adopt_image` | string |  | Also adopt running unlabeled containers of this image named after an instance id (taking over from another manager). |

## Use

### Fetch the binaries

```bash
pocketone docker update   # find the latest patch of each docker.versions minor, record and download it
pocketone docker seed     # download whatever is recorded but not in the cache yet
```

`update` checks upstream PocketBase releases (ganigeorgiev.com, then the archived GitHub) and PocketOne releases on
GitHub, verifies each download against the release's checksums.txt, and records the list in the cache's
`releases.json`. Run it when you want new patches. Nothing is downloaded at request time: when the host starts, any
listed release missing from the cache is downloaded in the background.

The cache layout is `<binaries>/<version>/<platform>/pocketbase` for PocketBase (PocketHost's existing layout) and
`<binaries>/p1/<version>/<platform>/pocketone` for PocketOne.

### Run the host

```bash
pocketone serve
```

- A container starts on an instance's first request and is ready when `/api/health` answers. At most
  `max_concurrent_starts` start at once.
- It stops after `idle_ttl` without requests.
- It restarts on its next request when what it runs changed (secrets, version, mounts). A change to routing only
  doesn't restart it.
- It stops when the instance is deleted or moves to another edge.
- Containers keep running when the host restarts; the next process adopts them by their labels.

### Hooks and migrations

A change in an instance's `pb_hooks` restarts its container. PocketBase's own hooks watcher stays on too, so a hook
file that fails to load is logged and skipped instead of stopping the instance. A request that arrives while the
instance restarts waits for it instead of failing; one that lost its connection mid-restart is sent once more if
it's safe to repeat (GET, HEAD or OPTIONS without a body). Migrations run when a container boots.

### Maintenance

Instance folders are ordinary folders under `root`. To work on one while nothing has it open, a host's Go code calls
`WithInstanceStopped` (below); requests for that instance wait up to 30 s, then get a 503 with `Retry-After`.

### Remote control

Containers run stock images with no PocketOne extensions, so the host answers
[remote/v1](https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/blob/main/ext/contracts/remote/v1/remote.go) for them at `/api/_c/remote/v1/` on each instance's hostname: the
`pocketone remote` commands work the same as against a Pocker instance or a single app. It answers after the host's
gates (firewall, rate limits) and blocked check, so a blocked instance's remote/v1 gets the blocked answer and the
container stays stopped.

- `GET /api/_c/remote/v1` (whoami) is public and lists `remote/v1`.
- `status`, `restart` and `logs` need a superuser token of that instance (`pocketone remote login` with a superuser
  email and password). The host asks the instance itself to check it.
- A host with its own accounts sets `docker.Provider.RemoteAuth` to decide who may call them instead (PocketHost: the
  instance owner's tokens). `remote/v1` is provided on the host's scope, so whoami also lists the other contracts the
  host provides for its instances (a host's `deploy/v1`).
- `restart` replaces the container; `logs` replays and follows the container's output, the last 1000 lines per
  instance kept by this host since it started following the container.

### Switching provider

Docker and Pocker both use `<root>/<id>`, so switching is a config change. Stop the containers first when leaving
docker, since they keep running across a host restart on purpose. Data only moves forward: an instance started on a
newer PocketBase than wrote its data is upgraded.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | Docker is a runtime provider of the host: the host routes by hostname, runs the listeners and gates, and hands each request to docker. |
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | The other provider. A host runs one or the other, over the same instance folders. |
| [Edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge) | For a fleet: requests for instances on another edge are forwarded there. |
| [Mothership](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mothership) | Instances (and their versions) come from a mothership instead of a file. |
| [Firewall](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall) | Rate limits and allow lists in front of every instance. |
| [Remotes](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/remotes) | The host provides remote/v1 for every container, so the CLI's whoami, status, restart and logs work. |

### Building on Docker

- **`docker.Provider`** fields extend the provider from Go: `Container` adds mounts, environment and labels to each
  container; `Version` rewrites an instance's version before the binary is picked; `OnLog` receives container output
  (default: the debug log); `Versions` replaces the `versions` list (for example a fleet's list from a mothership);
  `MinUpstream` replaces `min_upstream`.
- **`Spec`** (what `Container` fills in): `Binds`, `Env`, `Labels`, plus `Cmd` to adjust the command (for example
  drop a flag an old release lacks) and `HealthPath` / `HealthAnyStatus` for the readiness check.
- **`VersionsSource`**: any type with `Releases(ctx)` decides which releases the host serves, each pinned to its
  download and sha256. `YAMLVersions` (the `versions` key) is the built-in one.
- **Runtime API**: `docker.New(docker.Config{...})` builds the runtime without the config file.
  `WithInstanceStopped(ctx, id, fn)` stops an instance, holds its requests and runs `fn` on its folder (for deploys
  and restores); `StartInstance` starts one now; `InstanceDir` returns its folder. `Remote(host, dir)` and `SuperuserAuth()` are the
  remote/v1 provider and the host-side auth that `Provider` wires in, for a host built by hand
  (`remotev1.W.HostHandler(host, multisite.InstanceID, rt.SuperuserAuth(), next)` in `Host.InstanceRoutes`).
- **Release helpers**: `ParseVersion`, `Pick` / `PickMin`, `LatestPatches`, `Update` and `Seed` are what the commands
  use.

## Example

A minimal docker host: instances from a YAML file, each in its own container, routed by hostname on one listener. With
a Docker daemon running, start it from this folder with
`go run ./example --instances instances.yaml --data ./instances --binaries ./bin --versions pb:0.23,p1:0.0`.

```go
// A minimal docker host: instances from a YAML file, each in its own container with the PocketBase or PocketOne
// version it asks for, routed by hostname on one listener.
//
//	go run ./example --instances instances.yaml --data ./instances --binaries ./bin --versions pb:0.23,p1:0.0
//
// instances.yaml:
//
//	instances:
//	  - { id: blog, hosts: [blog.localhost], version: "pb:0.23.*" }
//	  - { id: shop, hosts: [shop.localhost], version: "p1:0.0.*" }
package main

import (
	"context"
	"flag"
	"log/slog"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"strings"
	"syscall"

	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/docker"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/multisite"
)

func main() {
	instances := flag.String("instances", "instances.yaml", "instances file")
	data := flag.String("data", "./instances", "folder with one folder per instance")
	binaries := flag.String("binaries", "./bin", "PocketBase and PocketOne binary cache")
	versions := flag.String("versions", "pb:0.23,p1:0.0", "minors to serve (latest patch each; fetched at start)")
	image := flag.String("image", "alpine:3.20", "base image")
	listen := flag.String("listen", "127.0.0.1:8090", "listen address")
	flag.Parse()

	b := &docker.Binaries{Root: *binaries}
	tracked := strings.Split(*versions, ",")
	if err := docker.RunUpdate(context.Background(), os.Stdout, docker.DefaultDiscovery(), b, tracked); err != nil {
		slog.Error("versions", "error", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	rt, err := docker.New(docker.Config{Image: *image, DataRoot: *data, Binaries: b, Versions: docker.YAMLVersions{Tracked: tracked, Root: b.Root}})
	if err != nil {
		slog.Error("docker", "error", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
	ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer stop()
	h := &multisite.Host{Source: &multisite.YAMLSource{Path: *instances}, Runtimes: []multisite.Runtime{rt}, Listeners: multisite.Listeners{Listen: *listen}}
	if err := h.Run(ctx); err != nil {
		slog.Error("host", "error", err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}
```

## How it works

- Each instance folder is mounted at `/home/pockethost` and the binary read-only at `/home/pockethost/pocketbase`.
  The container runs `./pocketbase serve --http 0.0.0.0:8090`, plus `--dev` for dev instances and
  `--encryptionEnv=PB_ENCRYPTION_KEY` when the instance has an encryption key. Its secrets are its environment.
- The port is published on 127.0.0.1 and the host proxies to it. This is the layout PocketHost's Node edge uses, so
  its instance folders and binary cache move as they are.
- Every container carries labels: `p1.runtime`, `p1.instance`, `p1.version` (the resolved release, such as
  `pb:0.36.9`) and `p1.spec` (a hash of its configuration, used to tell when it must restart). `adopt_image` also
  adopts unlabeled containers of an image, for taking over from another manager.
- Docker is reached over its socket API directly; there's no Docker SDK dependency.

### Status

Tested against a real Docker daemon, with upstream PocketBase 0.23 and PocketOne 0.0.1 side by side, alone and as a
host's runtime. Not yet in production.

`go test ./...` runs the Docker tests when a daemon is reachable (they're skipped with `-short`). The first run
downloads an upstream release and a PocketOne release into the user cache.

## License

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/sandbox

# Sandbox

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Confines one PocketOne app's JS hooks and migrations, so apps from people you don't know can share one process.
File access stays inside the app's folder, host primitives are gone, every JS call has a time limit, raw SQL can't
leave the app's own database files, and outbound connections reach public addresses only.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Sandbox isn't a switch in `pocketone`: [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) applies it to every instance it runs. With
a `multisite` section in `pocketone.yaml` (pocker as the runtime), every instance is sandboxed and there's nothing to install. A single app
served by `pocketone` without a `multisite` section is not sandboxed.

In your own Go build, give it to the [JSVM](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/jsvm) engine as an extension:

```go
sb := &sandbox.Sandbox{Dir: dir, Env: map[string]string{"GREETING": "hi"}}
execution, sleep := sb.Limits()
jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{
	HooksDir:   filepath.Join(dir, "pb_hooks"),
	Extensions: []any{sb},
	VM:         jsvm.VMConfig{TaskWall: execution, MaxSleep: sleep},
})
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/sandbox`. The SQL guard and the outbound network rules are
separate calls (see Integrations).

## Configure

Sandbox has no `pocketone.yaml` section of its own. Under Pocker its limits are set in the `pocker` section, as
defaults for every instance, and each instance can override them in its own `limits`:

```yaml
pocker:
  max_js_execution: 30s       # each JS call (hook, route, cron, migration) is interrupted after this
  max_js_allocation: 64MiB    # biggest single file read or reader JS can ask for
  max_call_stack_size: 2000   # unused: the JS engine caps its stack by size
  max_sleep: 10s              # cap on sleep()
  max_query_duration: 30s     # deadline for SQL statements that have none
  http_send_max_timeout: 60s  # cap on $http.send timeouts
  http_send_max_body: 10MiB   # cap on $http.send response size
  max_concurrent_js: 16       # JS calls one instance runs at once
  egress_allow: []            # private networks apps may still reach, such as an internal SMTP relay
```

The values shown are Pocker's defaults. An instance gets only its own `secrets` as environment.

In a Go build, the same settings are `Sandbox` fields: `Dir` (required), `Env`, `MaxExecution` (default 30 s,
negative turns it off), `MaxSleep`, `MaxAllocation`, `HTTPSendMaxTimeout`, `HTTPSendMaxBody`, and `Console` to send
`console.*` output somewhere other than the process's stdout and stderr. `Limits()` gives the execution and sleep
limits for `jsvm.Config.VM`; the memory cap and `MaxConcurrent` are set there too.

## Use

There's nothing to operate day to day. Hooks that stick to normal app code (`routerAdd`, `onRecord*`, `cronAdd`,
`$app.findRecordById` and the rest) run unchanged. What changes for a hook author:

- `$os.cmd`, `$os.exec`, `$os.exit` and `$filesystem.local` fail with "not available on this host (sandboxed)";
  `$os.args` is empty; process-wide Go methods such as `$app.restart` read as `undefined`.
- Files outside the app's folder can't be read or written, by any API, including through `..` or symlinks.
- `$os.getenv` and `process.env` see only the app's own environment.
- A JS call that runs past its time limit is interrupted with an error; so is one that asks for a huge allocation.
- `$http.send` to a private or loopback address is refused.

Under Pocker, `console.*` output and hook errors go to the instance's own `logs/exec.log`.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | Runs every instance through the sandbox, the SQL guard and the outbound network rules, with limits from the `pocker` section and each instance's `limits`. Its attack tests are in [`sandbox_test.go`](../pocker/sandbox_test.go). |
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | Carries the per-instance `limits` from `instances.yaml` or a mothership. |
| [Firewall](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall) | Rate and concurrency limits in front of every request. |
| [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) | The alternative for untrusted apps: a container per instance instead of checks inside one process. Docker doesn't use the sandbox. |

### Building on Sandbox

- **`Sandbox`** is a jsvm extension (`OnInit`, `Modules`, `HTTPClient`, and `HideField`/`HideMethod` to hide
  process-reaching Go members); add it to `jsvm.Config.Extensions`.
- **`GuardedDBConnect(maxQuery)`** is a `core.DBConnectFunc`: set it as the app's `DBConnect` to open the databases
  through SQLite's authorizer, with a deadline for statements that have none.
- **`InstallEgressPolicy(sandbox.EgressPolicy{Allow: ...})`** routes Go's default HTTP transport through the
  public-only dialer, for the whole process. `EgressPolicy.Dialer()` gives the same check for your own connections.
- **`BindMail(app)`** sends the app's own SMTP through that dialer.
- **`ErrSandboxed`** is the error disabled bindings return.

## Example

One app whose JS hooks are sandboxed: file access confined to the app folder, host primitives disabled, and a 5 s
limit per JS call. Run it from this folder with `go run ./example serve`.

```go
// Command example runs one PocketOne app whose JS hooks are sandboxed: file access is confined to the app folder,
// host primitives ($os.exec, $os.exit, ...) are disabled, and every JS call has a time limit.
//
//	go run ./example serve
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"log"
	"os"
	"path/filepath"
	"time"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/jsvm"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/sandbox"
)

func main() {
	app := pocketbase.New()
	devusers.Register(app) // local testing: superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"

	dir, _ := os.Getwd()
	sb := &sandbox.Sandbox{
		Dir:          dir,                                 // JS may only touch this folder
		Env:          map[string]string{"GREETING": "hi"}, // the only environment JS sees
		MaxExecution: 5 * time.Second,
	}

	jsvm.MustRegister(app, jsvm.Config{
		HooksDir:   filepath.Join(dir, "pb_hooks"),
		Extensions: []any{sb}, // OnInit, Modules, HTTPClient and the member filter
	})

	if err := app.Start(); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## How is this safe?

With [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker), PocketOne can serve hundreds of instances from one Go process, each with its own owner, hooks and data.
This section explains why that's safe enough to run code from people you don't know, and where it isn't.

Configuration and the engine API are in [POCKER.md](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker/pocker). The attack tests are in [`sandbox_test.go`](../pocker/sandbox_test.go).

### Why one process

Most hosted PocketBase instances are idle most of the time. A container per instance means paying idle memory and a
cold start of a second or more for each one. In one process an instance's app starts on its first request in tens of
milliseconds, costs a few MB while it runs, and shares the Go runtime with everyone else.

What you give up is the kernel boundary between tenants. Everything below replaces it with checks inside the process.

### The threat

Assume every instance's owner is hostile. They control:
- their `pb_hooks` (JavaScript, run by the instance's own QuickJS VM, [ext/jsvm](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/jsvm));
- their `pb_migrations`;
- their collections, rules and settings;
- any SQL their hooks run;
- requests to their own instance.

They must not be able to:
- read or change another instance's files, database, environment or settings;
- read the host's files, environment, credentials or private network;
- take the process down, or starve everyone else of CPU and memory.

### The layers

#### 1. Each instance is its own app

- Every instance has its own `core.App`, database, settings, JS VMs, migrations list, settings encryption key and
  log.
- Requests are routed by hostname to exactly one app. Nothing in one app holds a reference to another.
- In production only hostnames the instance source maps are served; unknown hosts get 404 and never create a folder.

#### 2. Files: confined by the kernel, not by string checks

Every file API reachable from JS goes through an `os.Root` opened on the instance's folder. That covers:
- `$os.*`
- `$filepath.glob`/`walk`
- `$filesystem.fileFromPath`
- `$template.loadFiles`
- `$apis.static`
- `require()`

The kernel resolves each path beneath that root and refuses `..` and symlinks that lead out. There is no path
string for an attacker to get clever with.

#### 3. Host primitives: removed

The following are gone from JS:
- process control: `$os.cmd`, `$os.exec`, `$os.exit`, `$os.args`;
- `$filesystem.local`;
- PocketBase internals that reach the whole process: `$app.restart`, `bootstrap`, `onServe`, `onTerminate`, raw
  `hook` triggers, `*sql.DB` handles;
- Go's `os/exec`, `net`, `syscall` and `database/sql/driver`.

A field-name mapper hides them, so they read as `undefined`. Everything a normal app uses still works: `routerAdd`,
`onRecord*`, `cronAdd`, `$app.findRecordById` and the rest.

#### 4. Environment: only the instance's own

`$os.getenv` and `process.env` return the instance's own secrets and nothing else. Platform values never go through
the environment:
- the settings encryption key;
- superusers the host keeps in sync;
- private tokens for the host's Go code.

#### 5. SQL: SQLite's own authorizer

Raw SQL is allowed (`$app.db().newQuery(...)`), because PocketBase apps depend on it. Instead of parsing statements,
PocketOne installs SQLite's authorizer callback on every connection, so SQLite itself refuses:
- `ATTACH` and `VACUUM INTO` outside the instance's `pb_data`;
- `load_extension`;
- the pragmas that move SQLite's files elsewhere.

Statements without a deadline get one (`max_query_duration`).

#### 6. Outbound network: public addresses only

PocketOne installs one dialer process-wide, on Go's default HTTP transport and PocketBase's SMTP client. It covers:
- `$http.send`
- `$filesystem.fileFromURL`
- S3 storage and backups
- OAuth2/JWKS fetches
- SMTP

The dialer refuses:
- loopback, private ranges, link-local and cloud metadata;
- CGNAT, multicast, reserved and documentation ranges;
- the IPv6 forms of all of these, including IPv4-in-IPv6.

It checks the address actually connected to, after DNS, so DNS rebinding doesn't help. `$http.send` timeouts and
response sizes are capped.

#### 7. CPU, memory and concurrency

| Resource | What's enforced |
|---|---|
| CPU | Every JS call (hook, route, cron, migration) is interrupted after `max_js_execution`, Go calls included. `sleep()` is capped. |
| Concurrency | At most `max_concurrent_js` JS calls per instance in flight at once; more wait, then fail. Per-IP and per-instance rate and concurrency limits sit in front of every request. |
| Memory | Each instance's VM has a hard cap (default 64 MiB): the JS heap plus the Go objects JS holds. A script that grows past it, slowly or at once, gets an out-of-memory error; other instances are unaffected. The JS stack is capped by size, so deep recursion is an error, never a crash. File reads are capped at `max_js_allocation`. |

Every limit has a process default and a per-instance override.

#### 8. Failures stay with their instance

- A broken hooks file, a panic during start or a failed migration fails that instance alone: it answers 502 and logs
  to its own `logs/exec.log`. Every other instance keeps serving.
- `console.*` output goes to the instance's own log, never to the host's.

### What it doesn't cover

Be clear about these before you host strangers:

- **Go memory is estimated.** Go objects JS holds are charged to the instance by estimate, and Go's garbage collector
  can let the process use up to about twice that; set `GOMEMLIMIT` for the process.
- **It's one address space.** A bug in Go, QuickJS, SQLite or PocketOne's own checks would cross tenants in a way a
  container boundary wouldn't. The sandbox tests cover the known paths, but they don't prove nothing else exists.
- **No OS-level layer yet.** Seccomp, Landlock and a second, OS-level egress filter aren't built in.

### How to run it

For untrusted tenants, add the OS layers yourself:
- run PocketOne as a non-root user that owns only the instances folder;
- run it under a cgroup memory limit (with swap), so the worst case is a restart, not a host OOM;
- add an OS firewall rule that lets that user reach public addresses only, an egress layer independent of the
  process;
- keep secrets for host code out of the process environment; use `private:` values instead;
- put a proxy or the built-in firewall in front, with rate limits on.

If you only run your own apps, the defaults are already more than stock PocketBase gives you.

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall

# Firewall

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Peer allow-lists, trusted proxies and client IPs, and per-IP and per-instance rate limits for a
[Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite), with or without [Edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge). Every request is checked before an instance
serves it or it's forwarded to another edge.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

The firewall is built into `pocketone`. It turns on in host mode (a `multisite` section in `pocketone.yaml`), as the host's [gate/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/gate/v1), when the file has
a `firewall` or `rate_limits` section; there's nothing else to install.

In your own Go build, importing the package registers it with the host, with the same rule:

```go
import _ "github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/firewall"
```

Or build one in Go and add it to the host's gates, as [the example](#example) does.

A single app doesn't need it: stock PocketBase has its own per-IP rate limits and trusted proxies.

## Configure

Two sections, both optional; either one turns the firewall on (keys below).

```yaml
firewall:
  allow_cidrs: []                 # peers allowed to connect (empty = everyone)
  trusted_proxies: []             # peers whose client-IP headers are believed
  client_ip_headers: [CF-Connecting-IP, True-Client-IP, X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP]
  trusted_clients: []             # client IPs that get the trusted rate limits on every instance
  trusted_client_headers: [X-Client-IP] # a trusted client names its end user: each user gets their own limits
  rate_limit_header_prefix: X-RateLimit
rate_limits:                      # defaults for every instance
  ip_hourly: 1000
  instance_hourly: 10000
  ip_concurrent: 15
  instance_concurrent: 250
  file_weight: 0.1                # a /api/files request costs a tenth
  trusted: { ip_hourly: 5000, instance_hourly: 20000, ip_concurrent: 50, instance_concurrent: 250 }
  # off: true                     # no rate limiting
```

The values shown are the defaults. In dev mode (`instances: { dev: true }`) rate limiting is off unless the file has a
`rate_limits` section. A trusted limit is never lower than the normal one.

Each instance can set its own limits and trusted IPs in its `extensions.firewall` settings; missing fields keep the
defaults:

```yaml
instances:
  - id: api
    hosts: [api.example.com]
    extensions:
      firewall: { rate_limits: { ip_hourly: 5000, instance_concurrent: 500 }, trusted_ips: [203.0.113.0/24] }
```

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `firewall:`

Peers allowed to connect, trusted proxies and client-IP headers, trusted clients, the rate-limit header prefix. Turns the firewall on.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `allow_cidrs` | list of string |  | Peers (IPs or CIDRs) allowed to connect; others get 403. Empty: everyone. |
| `trusted_proxies` | list of string |  | Peers whose client-IP headers are believed. |
| `client_ip_headers` | list of string |  | Headers read, in order, for the client IP from a trusted proxy. Default CF-Connecting-IP, True-Client-IP, X-Forwarded-For, X-Real-IP. |
| `trusted_clients` | list of string |  | Client IPs or CIDRs that get the trusted rate limits on every instance. |
| `trusted_client_headers` | list of string |  | Headers a trusted client uses to name its end user's IP, so each user gets their own limits. Default X-Client-IP. |
| `rate_limit_header_prefix` | string |  | Prefix of the rate-limit response headers. Default X-RateLimit. |

#### `rate_limits:`

Default rate limits for every instance (per instance: extensions.firewall.rate_limits). Turns the firewall on.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `ip_hourly` | int |  | Requests per hour from one client IP to one instance. Default 1000. |
| `instance_hourly` | int |  | Requests per hour to one instance from everyone. Default 10000. |
| `ip_concurrent` | int |  | Requests one client IP may have open on one instance at once. Default 15. |
| `instance_concurrent` | int |  | Requests one instance may have open at once. Default 250. |
| `file_weight` | number |  | What a /api/files request costs, as a share of a request. Default 0.1. |
| `trusted.ip_hourly` | int |  | Requests per hour from one trusted client IP to one instance. |
| `trusted.instance_hourly` | int |  | Requests per hour to one instance. |
| `trusted.ip_concurrent` | int |  | Requests one trusted client IP may have open on one instance at once. |
| `trusted.instance_concurrent` | int |  | Requests one instance may have open at once. |
| `off` | bool |  | No rate limiting. The default in dev mode unless rate_limits is set. |

## Use

What callers see:

- **Peers outside `allow_cidrs`** get 403.
- **Client IP:** taken from `client_ip_headers` only when the peer is a trusted proxy; otherwise it's the peer. The
  app then sees that client as the request's IP, so PocketBase's logs and its own rate limits see the visitor.
- **Over a limit:** 429 with `Retry-After` and a message naming the limit and the IP.
- **Every routed response** carries `X-RateLimit-{Ip,Instance}-{Hourly,Concurrent}-{Limit,Remaining}` and
  `X-RateLimit-{Ip,Instance}-Hourly-Reset` (with your prefix), listed in `Access-Control-Expose-Headers` so browser
  code can read them.
- **Long-lived responses** (realtime) count toward the concurrency limits until they end.

### Trusted clients that serve many users

A trusted client (process-wide `trusted_clients`, or an instance's own `trusted_ips`) that serves many users, such as
a server-side proxy or SSR app, sends each request's end-user IP in a `trusted_client_headers` header. Per-IP limits
then apply to that user, still with the trusted limits; without the header all its users share one bucket. The header
is ignored from anyone else, so it can't be spoofed to escape a limit.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | The firewall is a host gate: it checks the peer, then admits each request before the runtime or the forward hook. |
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker), [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) | Either provider; the firewall runs in front of both. |
| [Edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge) | The entry edge applies the limits before forwarding. The owner edge's rate-limit headers replace the entry edge's, since the owner counted every request for the instance. |
| [Multitenant](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tenants) (planned) | Will write each instance's `extensions.firewall` settings, such as its owner's trusted IPs. |

### Building on the firewall

- **Per instance.** Write `extensions.firewall.rate_limits` and `extensions.firewall.trusted_ips` into an instance's
  settings (from the instances file or your own instance source).
- **Go API.** `firewall.Firewall{Config, RateLimits}` is a `multisite.Gate` you can add to `Host.Gates` yourself;
  `NewFirewall(cfg)` builds one ready to use. `ClientIP(r)` gives a request's client. `firewall.SectionAdjust` changes
  the settings read from `pocketone.yaml` before the firewall is built.

## Example

The firewall in front of a toy host: only `127.0.0.1` may connect, at 100 requests an hour per IP. Run it from this
folder with `go run ./example --instances instances.yaml`.

```go
// The firewall in front of a host: every request is checked (allowed peers, rate limits) before a toy runtime
// answers. In a PocketOne binary the firewall turns on from pocketone.yaml's firewall / rate_limits sections; here
// it is built in Go.
//
//	go run ./example --instances instances.yaml
package main

import (
	"context"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"net/http"
	"os"
	"os/signal"
	"syscall"

	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/multisite"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/firewall"
)

type okRuntime struct{}

func (okRuntime) Name() string                        { return "ok" }
func (okRuntime) Serves(inst multisite.Instance) bool { return true }
func (okRuntime) Ready() bool                         { return true }
func (okRuntime) ServeInstance(w http.ResponseWriter, _ *http.Request, inst multisite.Instance) {
	fmt.Fprintf(w, "hello from %s\n", inst.ID)
}

func main() {
	instances := flag.String("instances", "instances.yaml", "instances file")
	listen := flag.String("listen", "127.0.0.1:8090", "listen address")
	flag.Parse()
	fw := &firewall.Firewall{
		Config:     firewall.Config{AllowCIDRs: []string{"127.0.0.1"}},
		RateLimits: &firewall.RateLimits{IPHourly: 100},
	}
	ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt, syscall.SIGTERM)
	defer stop()
	h := &multisite.Host{Source: &multisite.YAMLSource{Path: *instances}, Runtimes: []multisite.Runtime{okRuntime{}}, Gates: []multisite.Gate{fw}, Listeners: multisite.Listeners{Listen: *listen}}
	if err := h.Run(ctx); err != nil {
		fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, err)
		os.Exit(1)
	}
}
```

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge

# Edge

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

The fleet layer for a [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite): several servers (edges) share one set of instances, any edge accepts
any request, and a request for an instance another edge runs is forwarded there over the private network. Works with
either runtime provider, [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) or [docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker).

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Edge is built into `pocketone`. It turns on in host mode (a `multisite` section in `pocketone.yaml`) when the file has an
`edges` section, or a `mothership` section ([Mothership](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mothership)), which lists the edges too.

In your own Go build, give the host a router as its forward hook:

```go
edges, err := edge.FromSection(log) // the `edges` section; nil when there is none
if edges != nil {
	opts.Forward = edge.NewRouter(edge.RouterConfig{Edges: edges, Logger: log}).Forward
}
h, err := multisite.FromConfig(opts)
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/edge`.

## Configure

The `edges` section names this edge and lists the others (keys below):

```yaml
edges:
  self: lax-1
  list:
    - { id: sgp-1, internal_url: "http://10.88.0.4:8080", region: sgp }
server:
  plain: [":8080"]   # where the other edges reach this one (their internal_url for it)
```

Each entry needs `id` and `internal_url`. An instance another edge runs names its owner in `remote`:

```yaml
instances:
  - id: shop
    hosts: [shop.example.com]
    remote: edge:@sgp-1     # also accepted: edge:sgp-1, or sgp-1
```

Without a mothership, instances come from the instances file. With one, instances and edges both come from it; a
fixed `edges.list` entry wins over the mothership's for the same edge.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `edges:`

The fleet: this edge's id and a fixed list of the other edges (id, internal_url, region).

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `self` | string |  | This edge's id, such as lax-1. |
| `list` | list of object |  | The other edges: id, internal_url (where this edge reaches it) and optional region. |

## Use

There's nothing to run by hand. A load balancer sends visitors to any edge, and each request ends up on the edge that
runs its instance:

- **Owner healthy:** the request is forwarded to its `internal_url`, with the original hostname. An edge is healthy
  when its source heard from it in the last 30 seconds, or else when it answers `/.well-known/health` (an edge the
  source marks offline never is).
- **Owner briefly unreachable but healthy:** requests are held and retried every 250 ms until it answers. Only
  requests without a body (GET, HEAD, OPTIONS) are replayed after a failed connection.
- **Owner down or unknown:** a 503 with `Retry-After: 10`, at once.
- **Never bounced:** a request another edge already forwarded is never forwarded again; it gets a 421.
- **CORS:** for an instance with `access.cors_origins`, the entry edge answers preflights and sets the only
  `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` the browser sees.
- **Headers:** where both edges set the same header (such as the firewall's rate-limit headers), the owner's wins.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | Edge fills the host's forward hook for instances with `remote` set. |
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker), [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) | Either runs the instances this edge owns; an app already running here stops when its instance moves to another edge. |
| [Firewall](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/firewall) | The entry edge checks the peer and the instance's rate limits before forwarding. |
| [Mothership](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mothership) | Its mirror is an edge source: it follows the mothership's list of edges and their heartbeats. |

### Building on Edge

- **Edge sources.** Implement `edge.EdgeSource` (`Self`, `Resolve`, `Edges`) to say where the other edges are; add
  `Run` (`edge.Runner`) for background work. `YAMLProvider` is the `edges.list` one; `MultiProvider` combines several,
  the first to resolve an instance's `remote` winning.
- **Router.** `edge.NewRouter(edge.RouterConfig{...})` takes the health path, healthy window, retry interval and the
  503 and 421 messages. Plug `Router.Forward` into `multisite.Host.Forward`.
- **Timing.** `edge.WithMark(ctx)` records which edge a request was forwarded to and when, e.g. for Server-Timing.

## Example

Edge has no example program of its own. The stock binary wires it up in
[`examples/pocketone/multi.go`](../../examples/pocketone/multi.go), together with the mothership's edge list.

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mothership

# Mothership

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

A control plane for a fleet of edges. The mothership is a PocketOne app that records which edges exist and which
instances run where. Each edge follows it, serves its own instances and forwards requests for the rest to the edge
that runs them.

One operator, no users: owners and accounts are the [tenants](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tenants) extension (planned), which extends the
mothership through its collections and the mirror's extensions. Each layer is optional: an [edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge)
runs without a mothership, and a mothership without tenants.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

The edge side (the `mirror` package) is built into `pocketone`. It turns on when `pocketone.yaml` names a provider
and has a `mothership` section (below); `pocketone serve` then takes its instances and the other edges from the
mothership.

The mothership side has no switch yet. In the Go code of the PocketOne app that will be the mothership, create its
collections once the app has bootstrapped:

```go
if err := mothership.EnsureCollections(app); err != nil {
	return err
}
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/mothership`. In your own edge build, `mirror.FromSection(log)`
returns the mirror for the config (nil without a `mothership` section); use it as the host's instance source and the
router's edge source, as [`examples/pocketone/multi.go`](../../examples/pocketone/multi.go) does.

## Configure

On each edge, add a `mothership` section to the host's config; the mirror becomes the host's [instance.source/v1](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/instance.source/v1). Logins come from the private `.env`:

```yaml
multisite: {}
mothership:
  url: http://10.88.0.10:8090
  email: $MOTHERSHIP_EMAIL
  password: $MOTHERSHIP_PASSWORD
  self: lax-1                       # this edge's edge_id (or edges.self)
  internal_url: http://10.88.0.5:8080
  region: lax
  apex: example.com                 # <name>.example.com routes to each instance
```

`url` and `self` are required. The edge logs in as a superuser of the mothership.

On the mothership, there's nothing to configure beyond creating the collections.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `mothership:`

A community mothership to mirror instances and edges from: url, login, this edge's id, internal URL, region, apex.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `url` | string |  | The mothership's URL. Required. |
| `email` | string |  | Superuser email this edge logs in with; use a $VAR from the .env. |
| `password` | string |  | Superuser password; use a $VAR from the .env. |
| `self` | string |  | This edge's edge_id, such as lax-1. Default: the edges section's self. Required. |
| `internal_url` | string |  | Where other edges reach this one. Set: the edge registers itself when the mothership has no record for it. |
| `region` | string |  | Region recorded when the edge registers itself. |
| `apex` | string |  | Makes <name>.<apex> a hostname of every instance. Empty: hosts only. |
| `heartbeat` | duration |  | How often this edge marks itself online. Default 15s; negative: never. |
| `resync` | duration |  | How often everything is reloaded, in case a change was missed. Default 10m. |

## Use

You manage the fleet in the mothership's dashboard, in two collections only superusers can read or write:

- **`edges`**: `edge_id` (such as `lax-1`), `internal_url`, `region`, `status` (`online`, `draining`, `offline`) and
  `last_seen`. An edge with `internal_url` set registers itself when it has no record, marks itself online every
  15 s, and offline when it shuts down.
- **`instances`**: `name` (`<name>.<apex>` routes to it), `hosts` (extra hostnames), `edge` (where it runs),
  `power` (off answers 409 "instance is powered off"), `suspension` (non-empty answers 403 with that message), `dev`,
  `version`, `secrets`, `encryption_key`, `access`, `limits`, `plugins` (extension settings; the field keeps its old name) and `status`.

Changes reach the edges within moments over PocketBase's realtime stream; there's no polling. To move an instance,
change its `edge`: the old edge drops its full record and forwards to the new one until the new edge has it. An
instance with no `edge` isn't served anywhere.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | The mirror is the host's instance source: which instances exist and which this edge runs. |
| [Edge](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/edge) | The mirror is also an edge source: where the other edges are, so requests for their instances are forwarded. It combines with a fixed `edges` list. |
| [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) and [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | Run the instances this edge owns, with the version, secrets, limits and extension settings from each record. |
| [Tenants](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/tenants) (planned) | Adds owners and accounts through mirror extensions. |

### Building on Mothership

- **Your own fields and collections.** `EnsureCollections` leaves fields an extension added alone, so an extension can add
  its own fields and collections to the mothership.
- **Mirror extensions.** Pass a `mirror.Extension` to `mirror.FromSection` or `mirror.Config.Extensions`. `Views()`
  adds filtered subscriptions (such as `owners` filtered to `instances_via_owner.edge ?= {edge}`), `Instance()`
  adjusts each instance as it's built (block a suspended owner's instances, add an owner's trusted IPs), and
  `Changed()` names the instances a change in its views affects.
- **Go API.** `mirror.New(mirror.Config{...})` builds a mirror without the config file. `Get(view, id)` and
  `Records(view)` read any view; `SelfRecord()` is this edge's record id.

## Example

There's no `example/main.go` yet. The stock binary's multi-instance mode,
[`examples/pocketone/multi.go`](../../examples/pocketone/multi.go), follows a mothership when the config has the
section.

## How it works

Each edge subscribes to filtered views, so it only receives what concerns it:

| View | Collection | Filter / fields | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `edges` | edges | all | forwarding, and health from heartbeats |
| `routes` | instances | fields `id,name,hosts,edge,updated` | the routing table: any edge may get any visitor |
| `local` | instances | `edge = <this edge>` | full records (secrets, limits, plugins) for instances this edge runs |

An instance moving away shows up in `routes` and its full record is dropped; one moving here arrives in `local`. The
stream reconnects and reloads on its own, and reloads everything every 10 minutes in case anything was missed.

Filters cut what each edge downloads and keeps (most edges run a few of thousands of instances). They are not a
security boundary while edges log in as superusers.

### Status

Early. Built: the `edges` and `instances` collections (`EnsureCollections`) and the edge side (`mirror`). Not yet:
the mothership's own endpoints (placement, moves) and instance status reports.

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/schedules

# Schedules

Scheduled webhooks per instance, called in-process even while the instance sleeps, with a catch-up run after downtime.

**Runs on:** [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) (multitenant).

> **Planned.** Nothing is published here yet. This folder will hold the extension's Go module
> (`github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/schedules`), its tests and a minimal `example/main.go` that builds and shows the
> feature. See [Create your own extension](https://pocketone.dev/docs/writing-an-extension).

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Not available yet: Schedules isn't in `pocketone` and has no Go module to add to a custom build.

## Configure

Nothing to configure yet. Its settings will be documented here when it ships.

## Use

Nothing to use yet. It is planned to let each instance schedule webhooks that fire on time even while the instance is asleep, and to run missed ones once after downtime.

## Integrations

It is planned to run on [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker), which hosts many instances in one process and calls each schedule without waking the instance first.

# Stats

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Looks after the data of the instances a host serves. Today it measures facts about each instance (disk used, last
request served) and reports them. Later it will also carry out decisions about that data, such as archiving.

> **Status.** Working, first step: facts and the `measure` decision. Archiving, restoring, offloading backups and
> purging come next, as further decisions. The [rules engine](#rules-criteria-an-app-can-replace) is ready as a Go
> library but isn't read from `pocketone.yaml` yet.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Lifecycle runs on a host that serves many instances ([ext/multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite), with [pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker)
or [docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker)), not on a single app.

The stock `pocketone` binary turns it on by itself in host mode: when `pocketone.yaml` has a `multisite` section,
every instance under the first runtime's root folder is measured. There's no switch to flip.

```yaml
multisite: {}
instances: { file: ./instances.yaml }
```

In your own host build, add it as a gate (to see requests) and a background job:

```go
lc := &stats.Lifecycle{Directory: h.Directory, Folder: func(i multisite.Instance) string { return filepath.Join(root, i.ID) }}
h.Gates = append(h.Gates, lc)                // records each local instance's last request
h.Background = append(h.Background, lc.Run) // measures and reports on the policy's schedule
```

`Folder` says where an instance's data lives. The stock binary uses the instance's own `dir` when it has one, else
`<root>/<id>`.

## Configure

The `lifecycle` section in `pocketone.yaml` sets the schedule. Everything is optional.

```yaml
lifecycle:
  measure_every: 24h   # how old a disk measurement may get
  report_every: 1h     # how often changed last-request times are reported
  concurrency: 2       # instances measured at once
```

### The policy

What to do comes from a policy. The built-in one (`YAMLPolicy`) reads this section and decides one thing: measure an
instance when it was never measured, or when its measurement is older than `measure_every`. Zero or missing values
fall back to the defaults.

Rules with criteria, `all`/`any`/`not`, vetoes and budgets exist in the [rules engine](#rules-criteria-an-app-can-replace),
but the `lifecycle` section doesn't take them yet.

### pocketone.yaml reference

#### `lifecycle:`

Instance data on this host: how often disk use is measured and last-request times are reported.

| Key | Type | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `measure_every` | duration | `24h0m0s` | How old an instance's disk measurement may get before it is measured again. Default 24h. |
| `report_every` | duration | `1h0m0s` | How often changed last-request times are reported to the sink. Default 1h. |
| `concurrency` | int | `2` | How many instances are measured at once. Default 2. |

## Use

### What it measures

For each instance this host serves itself (not the ones it forwards to another edge):

- `disk_bytes`: the size of the regular files in the instance's folder (symlinks aren't followed; 0 when there's no
  folder), and `measured_at`, when that was measured.
- `last_active`: the last request this host served for it, recorded at most once a minute per instance.

### When

- As soon as the instance list loads, every instance is measured, because none has been measured yet.
- After that it checks once a minute and measures the instances whose measurement is older than `measure_every`.
- Changed last-request times are reported every `report_every`.

Facts are kept in memory. With the default log sink, a restart measures everything again.

### What you'll see

Log lines from the default sink and the measuring pass:

```
INFO lifecycle: facts instances=12 disk_bytes=48213504
INFO lifecycle: measured instances=12 disk_bytes=48213504 ms=37
```

`lifecycle: facts` is each report the sink receives (after a measuring pass, and for last-request times).
`lifecycle: measured` follows a measuring pass, with how long it took. Problems show as warnings: `lifecycle:
measuring` (a folder couldn't be read), `lifecycle: report` (the sink failed; last-request times are retried next
time) and `lifecycle: policy`.

### Try it

[`example/main.go`](example/main.go) measures the instance folders under a root once and prints each instance's size:

```bash
go run ./example --root ./pb_root --instances instances.yaml
```

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Multisite](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/multisite) | Lifecycle is a `multisite.Gate` (it sees each request to record `last_active`) and a host background job (`Run`). It lists instances from `multisite.Directory`. |
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | Instances under `pocker.root` (default `./pb_root`), one folder per instance. |
| [Docker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/docker) | Instances under `docker.root`, the same `<root>/<id>` layout. |

It knows nothing about plans, payments or tenants: that belongs to whichever policy provider is configured.

### Your own policy

Set `Lifecycle.Policy` to anything that implements `PolicyProvider`:

```go
type PolicyProvider interface {
	Decide(ctx context.Context, facts []Facts) ([]Decision, error) // what to do now, and why
	ReportEvery() time.Duration                                    // how often last-request times are reported
	Concurrency() int                                              // instances worked on at once
}
```

A control plane can provide its own, for example one that delegates the decisions to a mothership, and providers can
wrap each other. Only the `measure` action is carried out today; any other action is logged as `lifecycle: action not
supported yet`.

### Your own sink

Set `Lifecycle.Sink` to anything that implements `Sink` (`Report(ctx, facts []Facts) error`) to send facts somewhere
other than the log. A sink that also implements `Loader` (`Load(ctx) ([]Facts, error)`) gives the facts back at start,
so a restart doesn't measure everything again or forget last-request times.

### Rules: criteria an app can replace

`rules` (package `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/stats/rules`, standard library only) is the engine policies
are built from, on an edge or a mothership. A subject is whatever the caller evaluates: an instance's facts on an
edge, an account with its instances on a mothership.

- **Criteria** answer one question about a subject (stale? orphaned? over its plan?) and say why. They live in a
  `Registry` by name: an app registers its own or replaces a built-in one (`Register("stale", ...)`), and every rule
  that refers to the name (`Ref("stale")`) follows, so what "stale" means is the app's to decide.
- **Where they come from** is pluggable too: code, or definitions from config (`Load`) built from kinds the app
  registered (`RegisterKind("idle", ...)`) and combined with `all`, `any` and `not`. A YAML section and a mothership
  are both just sources of definitions. `Load` registers nothing when a definition is wrong.
- **Rules** lead from a criterion to an action, with named vetoes that always win and a budget per run.
- **Reports** list each decision with its reasons, what was vetoed and by what, what the budget held back and what
  failed. `Summary` gives one line per rule (`archive-stale: 3 decided, 1 vetoed`). Evaluating does nothing by itself:
  acting on the decisions, or only logging them in a dry run, is the caller's.

A definition, as config would supply it:

```yaml
stale:      { kind: idle, params: { after: 8760h } }
archivable: { kind: all, of: [stale, free_plan] }
keep:       { kind: not, of: [archivable] }
```

And in Go:

```go
r := rules.NewRegistry[Facts]()
r.RegisterKind("idle", idleFor)                       // params: { after: 8760h }
_ = r.Load(map[string]rules.Def{
	"stale":      {Kind: "idle", Params: map[string]any{"after": "8760h"}},
	"archivable": {Kind: "all", Of: []string{"stale", "free_plan"}},
})
e := rules.Engine[Facts]{Key: id, Rules: []rules.Rule[Facts]{{
	Name: "archive-stale", Action: "archive", When: r.Ref("archivable"),
	Unless: []rules.Veto[Facts]{{Name: "pinned", If: r.Ref("pinned")}}, Budget: 200,
}}}
report := e.Evaluate(ctx, facts)
```

Every rule sees every subject, so one subject can get several decisions. Make rules exclusive by building them from
exclusive criteria.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](example/main.go) measures the instance folders under a root once and prints their facts, which is what a host's lifecycle does daily.

```go
// Measure the instance folders under a root once and print their facts (what a host's lifecycle does daily).
//
//	go run ./example --root ./pb_root --instances instances.yaml
package main

import (
	"context"
	"flag"
	"fmt"
	"log"
	"log/slog"
	"path/filepath"

	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/multisite"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/stats"
)

func main() {
	root := flag.String("root", "./pb_root", "one folder per instance: <root>/<id>")
	instances := flag.String("instances", "instances.yaml", "instances file")
	flag.Parse()

	src := &multisite.YAMLSource{Path: *instances, Required: true}
	list, err := src.Snapshot(context.Background())
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
	dir := multisite.NewDirectory(slog.Default())
	dir.Load(list)

	lc := &stats.Lifecycle{
		Directory: dir,
		Folder: func(i multisite.Instance) string {
			if i.Dir != "" {
				return i.Dir
			}
			return filepath.Join(*root, i.ID)
		},
		Sink: stats.LogSink{},
	}
	lc.Step(context.Background()) // never measured: every instance is measured now
	for _, f := range lc.Local() {
		fmt.Printf("%-24s %12d bytes\n", f.Instance, f.DiskBytes)
	}
}
```

## How it works

- Go module `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/stats`. The stock binary wires it in
  [`examples/pocketone/multi.go`](../../examples/pocketone/multi.go).
- `Run` loads recorded facts from a `Loader` sink, then waits for the host's instance list to load (checking every
  second). From then on, once a minute, it asks the policy for decisions on the current facts, measures the instances
  it was asked to (`concurrency` at a time) and reports what it measured to the sink.
- Measuring walks the folder and adds up regular file sizes. An instance's pending last-request time goes out with its
  measurement, so it isn't reported twice.
- `Admit` records `last_active` only for instances this host serves itself (`Remote` empty), and never refuses a
  request.

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailrelay

# Mail Relay

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

Outgoing mail for [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) instances that haven't set up SMTP.

Stock PocketBase falls back to the host's `sendmail` when SMTP is off. Under Pocker that would run `sendmail` on the
shared host for every tenant. With this extension:

- **SMTP on** in an instance's Settings → Mail: the app sends the mail itself. Bring your own SMTP always wins.
- **SMTP off:** the mail goes through your relay as `<instance>@<Domain>`, within per-instance limits. `sendmail`
  never runs.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

Mail Relay is not in the `pocketone` binary. Add it to the extensions of your own Pocker build, with your sending
domain and relay:

```go
srv.Extensions = append(srv.Extensions, mailrelay.New(mailrelay.Config{
    Domain:   "mail.example.com",
    Upstream: mailrelay.SMTPUpstream{Addr: "smtp.provider.com:587", Username: "…", Password: "…"},
}))
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/mailrelay`. It works the same in `pocker.Provider{Extensions: ...}`.
It also registers on a single app, but a single app can set up its own SMTP and doesn't need a relay.

## Configure

### The relay (Go)

`Domain` and `Upstream` are required; the host doesn't start without them.

- **`Domain`**: every relayed message is From `<local part>@Domain`.
- **`Upstream`**: what delivers the mail. `SMTPUpstream` ships here: `Addr` (host:port), optional `Username` and
  `Password` (PLAIN auth, only over TLS or to localhost), `ImplicitTLS` for port 465 (otherwise STARTTLS when the
  server offers it), and `Timeout` (default 30 s). It dials with its own dialer, so Pocker's egress rules for tenants
  (public addresses only) don't block a relay on a private address. Anything with
  `Send(ctx, from, to, raw)` works, for example an Amazon SES `SendRawEmail` sender.
- **`LocalPart`**: picks an instance's address from its id. The default is the first label of the id, lowercased:
  `blog.localhost` → `blog`.
- **Limits:** `PerMinute` (default 20) and `Daily` (default 200) per instance, `MaxRecipients` (To + Cc + Bcc,
  default 5) and `MaxSize` (encoded message, default 1 MiB) per message.

### Defaults for every instance (`pocketone.yaml`)

```yaml
mailrelay: { per_minute: 20, daily: 200 }
```

Limits set in Go win over this section. Each instance can override it (see [Per-instance settings](#per-instance-settings-pocker)).

## Use

Once it's in, there's nothing to run. Each instance's mail is relayed whenever its SMTP is off.

- **Settings → Mail** in an instance's dashboard shows its superusers the relay: the address it sends as, its limits
  and how many messages it sent today. When sending is off for the instance, it says so and points to the SMTP
  settings.
- **The app's log** (Admin > Logs, which Pocker copies to the instance's own log) gets one line per message, with
  masked addresses: `mailrelay: sent from=blog@… to=a***@x.org`. Refusals and upstream failures are warnings.
- **A refused message** returns an error to whoever triggered the mail, such as a password-reset request: sending
  off, too many recipients, too large, or the limit reached.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Contracts](https://pocketone.dev/docs/contracts/all) | Provides `mail.fallback/v1`: with SMTP off, an app's mail goes to the contract's providers in order (`providers: { mail.fallback/v1: [mailtrap, mailrelay] }`); Mail Relay sends it within the instance's limits. |
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | The host it's built for. Every instance gets the relay, its own address and its own limits. |
| [Mail Trap](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/mailtrap) | In development, point `SMTPUpstream` at the trap's SMTP port and every relayed message lands in one inbox, tagged with the instance. The example below does this. |
| [Bulk Mail](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/bulkmail) | Campaigns go through PocketBase's mailer by default, so with SMTP off they are relayed and count against the instance's limits. |

### Per-instance settings (pocker)

Each instance can override the defaults in its `extensions.mailrelay` settings, from `instances.yaml` or your instance
source (for example, per plan):

```yaml
instances:
  - id: free-plan-app
    extensions: { mailrelay: { send: false } }               # refuse its mail unless it uses its own SMTP
  - id: big-app
    extensions: { mailrelay: { per_minute: 60, daily: 2000 } }
```

A change to these settings restarts the instance's app on its next request.

Use `send: false`, not `enabled: false`, to stop an instance sending. `enabled: false` turns the extension off for that
instance, and with SMTP off PocketBase then falls back to the host's `sendmail`. Don't set it under Pocker.

### Building on Mail Relay

- **Your own upstream.** Implement `mailrelay.Upstream` (`Send(ctx, from, to, raw)`) to deliver through an API.
- **Your own hooks first.** The relay runs after the app's own `onMailerSend` hooks, so they can still change or
  drop a message.
- **Go API.** `(*mailrelay.Extension).Address(id)` returns the From address an instance sends as.
- **settings/v1** (superusers): `GET /api/_c/settings/v1/get?extension=mailrelay` returns the instance's relay status, a read-only section: `active`, `send`, `address`,
  `perMinute`, `daily`, `sentToday`.

## Example

[`example/main.go`](example/main.go) runs a Pocker host whose relay sends to the dev mail trap, so every instance's
mail lands in one inbox at http://127.0.0.1:8025. Run `go run ./example --dev` from this folder, then trigger a
password reset on any instance:

```bash
curl -X POST http://alpha.localhost:8090/api/collections/users/request-password-reset -d email=user@example.com
```

Log in to an instance's dashboard as `admin@example.com` / `password` to see the relay on Settings → Mail. `--listen`
changes the instances' port; `P1_MAILTRAP_HTTP` and `P1_MAILTRAP_SMTP` change the trap's.

```go
// Command example is a Pocker build with mailrelay, relaying into PocketOne's dev mail trap: every instance
// without its own SMTP sends as <instance>@mail.localhost, and all of it lands in one inbox.
//
//	go run ./example --dev
//
// Then trigger mail on any instance, for example a password reset (each instance has the test user below):
//
//	curl -X POST http://alpha.localhost:8090/api/collections/users/request-password-reset -d email=user@example.com
//	curl -X POST http://beta.localhost:8090/api/collections/users/request-password-reset -d email=user@example.com
//
// and read it in PocketOne's dev mail trap at http://127.0.0.1:8025 (filter by instance; P1_MAILTRAP_HTTP and
// P1_MAILTRAP_SMTP change its ports). Settings → Mail in each dashboard shows the relay.
//
// Logins (ext/devusers, local testing only): dashboard admin@example.com / password, app user user@example.com / password.
package main

import (
	"context"
	"flag"
	"log"
	"os"
	"os/signal"

	"ganigeorgiev.com/pocketbase/pocketbase/core"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/devusers"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/mailrelay"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/mailtrap"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/pocker"
	"github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/standard"
)

func main() {
	dev := flag.Bool("dev", false, "serve any hostname (alpha.localhost, beta.localhost, ...); otherwise instances.yaml is required")
	listen := flag.String("listen", "", "HTTP address for the instances (default :8090)")
	flag.Parse()

	cfg := pocker.DefaultConfig()
	cfg.Dev = cfg.Dev || *dev
	if *listen != "" {
		cfg.Listen = *listen
	}

	ctx, stop := signal.NotifyContext(context.Background(), os.Interrupt)
	defer stop()

	// The dev mail trap (ext/mailtrap) stands in for the operator's real relay (SES, a provider's SMTP, ...)
	inbox, err := mailtrap.Default("mailrelay example: the relay sends to the trap")
	if err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}

	srv := &pocker.Server{
		Config:   cfg,
		Standard: standard.New(), // every instance gets the standard extensions
		Extensions: []pocker.Extension{
			mailrelay.New(mailrelay.Config{
				Domain:   "mail.localhost",
				Upstream: mailrelay.SMTPUpstream{Addr: inbox.SMTPAddr},
			}),
		},
		// local testing: every instance gets superuser admin@example.com and user user@example.com, password "password"
		SetupApp: func(_ pocker.Instance, app core.App) error { return devusers.Ensure(app) },
	}
	if err := srv.Run(ctx); err != nil {
		log.Fatal(err)
	}
}
```

## How it works

- The extension binds PocketBase's `OnMailerSend` on every instance, last, after the app's own hooks. No core change.
- When SMTP is off it doesn't call `e.Next()`, so PocketBase's `sendmail` fallback never runs. It relays the message
  in-process instead.
- Nothing is written to the instance's settings. A backup restored somewhere else has no relay credentials in it, and
  falls back to stock PocketBase behavior.

For each message:

1. **Check it's allowed.** May this instance send (`send`)? Are there no more than 5 recipients (To + Cc + Bcc)? Is
   the encoded size no more than 1 MiB?
2. **Count it.** Each message counts once against the instance's limits, however many recipients it has. The day
   resets at midnight UTC. Counts are kept in memory.
3. **Set the sender.** The From address becomes `<local part>@<Domain>`. The display name is kept, minus anything
   that looks like an address or a link. The app's own sender address becomes `Reply-To`, unless it's PocketBase's
   `@example.com` placeholder.
4. **Build and send.** Bcc stays out of the headers. An `X-Pocker-Instance` header is added, then the message goes to
   the `Upstream`.
5. **Log it** to the app's log.

## License

MIT


---

Source: https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3-fallback

# S3 Fallback

Version 0.0.1 · Owners: [@benallfree](https://github.com/benallfree)

A default bucket for instances that have no S3 of their own. You name your S3-compatible backends once, then mount
each kind of file on one: record uploads, backup zips, PITR history, or any extension's own kind. Every instance gets
its own folder in the bucket and can't reach anything outside it. The credentials never reach the instance.

[Install](#install) · [Configure](#configure) · [Use](#use) · [Integrations](#integrations) · [Example](#example)

## Install

S3 Fallback isn't built into `pocketone`; add it to a Go build. Under [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker), add it to the
server's extensions:

```go
srv := &pocker.Server{Config: cfg, Extensions: []pocker.Extension{s3fallback.New(s3fallback.Config{})}}
```

On a single app, register it with the backends and mounts in Go:

```go
extkit.MustRegister(app, s3fallback.New(s3fallback.Config{Backends: backends, Mounts: mounts}))
```

The module is `github.com/pockethost/pocketone/ext/s3-fallback`.

## Configure

Under Pocker the `storage` section of `pocketone.yaml` is read at start. Fields set in Go win.

```yaml
storage:
  backends:                        # named S3-compatible destinations
    r2-eu:   { endpoint: https://<account>.eu.r2.cloudflarestorage.com, bucket: pocketbase-eu, region: auto, access_key: $R2_KEY, secret: $R2_SECRET }
    b2-cold: { endpoint: ..., bucket: ph-backups, region: ..., access_key: ..., secret: ... }
  mounts:                          # filesystem kind -> backend
    storage:    r2-eu              # record uploads
    backups:    b2-cold            # backup zips
    litestream: r2-eu              # PITR history (ext/pitr)
  # enabled: false                 # off for every instance
```

Each backend also takes `prefix` (prepended to every key, so several deployments can share a bucket) and
`force_path_style` (for MinIO and similar servers). With no mounts the extension does nothing and files stay on local
disk, as in PocketBase.

Each instance can turn it off in its own settings, from `instances.yaml` or a mothership. Only `enabled` is read per
instance; backends and mounts are the operator's:

```yaml
instances:
  - id: blog
    extensions: { storage: { enabled: false } }
```

The old shape (`bucket:` with `uploads:` / `backups:`) still works, with a warning: it becomes a backend named
`default`, mounted for uploads and backups.

## Use

There's nothing to do day to day. To an instance nothing is configured: Settings show S3 off, and uploads, thumbs,
`$app.newFilesystem()` and the Backups screen work as before. Files land in the bucket under
`<prefix>instances/<id>/<kind>/`. Downloads stream through the server, or redirect to the bucket with
[S3 Redirect](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3redirect).

When an instance turns on its own S3 (Settings → Files storage, or Settings → Backups), PocketBase's normal code takes
over with the instance's credentials. Files already in the default bucket stay there, as PocketBase's own S3 switch
doesn't move files either.

It applies to instances created with the extension on. Files already on an instance's local disk are not read or moved.

## Integrations

### Works with

| Extension | How they fit |
|---|---|
| [Pocker](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pocker) | Each instance gets the root `instances/<id>/`; the `storage` section is read when the server starts. |
| [PITR](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/pitr) | Mount `litestream` and every instance without its own bucket keeps its history there. An instance's own PITR bucket still wins. |
| [S3 Redirect](https://pocketone.dev/docs/extensions/s3redirect) | Downloads become signed redirects to the bucket. Nothing to wire: the fenced filesystem signs with its prefix, so S3 Redirect treats it like any S3 mount. |

### Building on S3 Fallback

- **Your own kind.** Any kind an extension asks for through PocketBase's `OnFilesystemCreate` is served when it's mounted.
  PITR's `litestream` works this way. Uploads and backups step aside when the app turned on its own S3; for other
  kinds, the extension asking checks its own app setting first.
- **Go API.** `Bind(app, root)` serves an app's filesystems from the mounts under `root` (`""` for a single app,
  `instances/<id>/` under Pocker). `FS(root, kind)` returns the same fenced filesystem outside a hook; close it when
  done. `Config()` returns the effective configuration.

## Example

There's no `example/main.go` yet. [`storage_test.go`](storage_test.go) and [`mounts_test.go`](mounts_test.go) show
it on a single app and under Pocker, against MinIO.

## How it works

- PocketBase asks `OnFilesystemCreate` before it creates a filesystem. For a mounted kind, the extension answers with the
  backend, fenced to `<backend prefix><root><kind>/`. An instance can't list, read, write or delete anything outside
  it.
- The fence is a driver that adds the prefix to every key and strips it from listings. Signed download URLs are made
  with the backend's own credentials.

### Status

Works and is tested against MinIO; not yet deployed.

## License

MIT
